percent-off.s1t: Separate a discount from a margin
percent-off.s1b: 20% off 100 means the buyer pays 80.00. A 20% margin on a selling price of 100 means the cost was 80 and the profit is 20. Same digits, different job.
percent-off.s2b: The arithmetic stays in this tab.
percent-off.s3t: Enter the list price and the percent off
percent-off.s3b: The price must be zero or more. 100 at 20% off is a sale price of 80.00 and a saving of 20.00. 80 at 25% off is 60.00 and 20.00.
percent-off.s4b: Both lines use two decimals. There is no currency. Copy both, then use the line the form named.
percent-off.s5t: A percent over 100 can go below zero
percent-off.s5b: 120% off 100 is a sale price of -20.00 and a saving of 120.00. That is arithmetic. A shop tag that cannot go below zero needs a different rule.
percent-off.s6t: A negative percent raises the price
percent-off.s6b: Minus 10% on 100 is a sale price of 110.00. The saving line is -10.00. If the tag says 10% off, the percent is 10, not -10.
percent-off.diagram1: 20% off 100: sale 80.00, saving 20.00. Not a 20% margin.
percent-off.diagram2: 120% off 100 is -20.00. Minus 10% raises the price to 110.00.

encode-url.name: How to encode a URL
encode-url.blurb: Encoding turns a space into %20 and also encodes slashes. Decoding turns + into a space. A broken % sequence fails.
encode-url.title: How to encode a URL
encode-url.lead: You have a string that must travel inside a URL. You will encode or decode it in this tab. Encoding the whole address also encodes the slashes. A query that uses + for a space decodes that plus as a space.
encode-url.result: A percent-encoded string, or the text decoded from one, including spaces that arrived as +.
encode-url.note: Open URL encode when the string is in front of you. Encode uses encodeURIComponent. Decode turns + into a space before reading % sequences. Nothing is uploaded.
encode-url.s1b: Encoding a query value is the usual job. Encoding https://cv.cm/a b also turns : and / into %3A and %2F. The result is one component, not an address you can open as-is.
encode-url.s2b: The string stays in this tab.
encode-url.s3b: Encode turns text into percent-encoding. Decode turns percent-encoding back into text. Encoding a string that is already encoded wraps it a second time.
encode-url.s4b: Encode writes a space as %20, not as +. Decode turns both %20 and + into a space. a+b decodes as a b.
encode-url.s5b: Each % must be followed by two hex digits. %zz and a lone % fail. Fix the pairs, then decode again.
encode-url.s6b: A space should come back as a space. A slash you encoded on purpose should come back as /. If the text is still full of % signs, it was encoded twice.
encode-url.diagram1: A space encodes as %20. A slash encodes as %2F. + decodes as a space.
encode-url.diagram2: % must have two hex digits. Encoding twice leaves the % signs in place.

calculate-age.name: How to calculate age
calculate-age.blurb: Count civil years, months, and days. Born 15 March 2000, on 14 March 2026 the age is still 25 years, 11 months, and 27 days.
calculate-age.title: How to calculate age
calculate-age.lead: You have a birth date and a later date. You will read years, months, days, and total days in this tab. The birthday that has not arrived yet does not add a year. A date before the birth date fails.
calculate-age.result: Years, months, and days on the civil calendar, plus the total day gap from the birth date to the later date.
calculate-age.note: Open age when both dates are real civil dates. The later date cannot be before the birth date. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-age.s1t: Wait for the birthday before adding a year
calculate-age.s1b: Born 15 March 2000, on 14 March 2026 the age is 25 years, 11 months, and 27 days. On 15 March 2026 it is 26 years, 0 months, and 0 days.
calculate-age.s2b: The count stays in this tab.
calculate-age.s3t: Enter the birth date and the later date
calculate-age.s3b: Both are civil dates, YYYY-MM-DD. A later date before the birth date fails. Today on this page is the calendar date of this computer, not a UTC clock time.
calculate-age.s4b: If the day of the month has not been reached, the count borrows the previous month. 14 March has not reached a 15 March birthday, so the years stay 25 and the months are 11.
calculate-age.s5t: Read total days as a gap
calculate-age.s5b: Total days do not count both ends. From 15 March 2000 to 14 March 2026 is 9,495 days. The next day, the birthday, is 9,496.
calculate-age.s6t: Keep 29 February as a real birth date
calculate-age.s6b: A leap-day birth is a civil date. On 28 February 2025, someone born 29 February 2000 is 24 years, 11 months, and 30 days. The birthday has not arrived.
calculate-age.diagram1: 15 Mar 2000 to 14 Mar 2026: 25 years, 11 months, 27 days.
calculate-age.diagram2: The next day is 26 years, 0 months, 0 days. Total days are a gap.

aspect-ratio.name: How to find an aspect ratio
aspect-ratio.blurb: Reduce whole pixels. 1920 by 1080 is 16:9. 1080 by 1920 is 9:16. Decimals are rounded before the ratio. This does not crop a photo.
aspect-ratio.title: How to find an aspect ratio
aspect-ratio.lead: You have a width and a height in pixels. You will reduce them in this tab. The order matters: 1920×1080 is 16:9, and 1080×1920 is 9:16. The page rounds to whole pixels first. It does not cut the picture.
aspect-ratio.result: A reduced ratio such as 16:9, plus the decimal width divided by height.
aspect-ratio.note: Open aspect ratio when you know the two pixel counts. Width and height must be greater than zero. Nothing is uploaded.
aspect-ratio.s1t: Keep width and height in order
aspect-ratio.s1b: 1920 wide and 1080 tall is 16:9. 1080 wide and 1920 tall is 9:16. A portrait frame and a landscape frame are not the same ratio.
aspect-ratio.s2b: The reduction stays in this tab.
aspect-ratio.s3t: Enter width and height in pixels
aspect-ratio.s3b: Both must be greater than zero. The page rounds each number to a whole pixel before it reduces. 1920 and 1080 become 16 and 9.
aspect-ratio.s4t: Read the reduced ratio and the decimal
aspect-ratio.s4b: 16:9 is the reduced pair. The decimal is width divided by height, about 1.7778 for 1920×1080. Copy keeps the ratio text.
aspect-ratio.s5b: A decimal pixel count becomes the nearest whole pixel. If the rounded pair is not the frame you meant, type the whole pixels from the file.
aspect-ratio.s6b: This page only reduces two numbers. 1920×1080 becomes 16:9 on the page, and the picture stays 1920 by 1080. Cropping is the crop tool.
aspect-ratio.diagram2: Round to whole pixels first. The photo is not cropped.

calculate-bmi.name: How to calculate BMI
calculate-bmi.blurb: 70 kg and 170 cm is a BMI of 24.2, in the Normal band. 1.70 in the centimetre box is 242214.5. 25 is Overweight and 30 is Obesity.
calculate-bmi.title: How to calculate BMI
calculate-bmi.lead: You have a weight and a height. You will read a BMI to one decimal and a band in this tab. The weight is kilograms. The height is centimetres. 70 kg and 170 cm is 24.2. The same weight with 1.70 in the centimetre box is 242214.5.
calculate-bmi.result: A BMI to one decimal, and one adult band: Underweight, Normal, Overweight, or Obesity.
calculate-bmi.note: Open BMI when both numbers are above zero. The page uses kilograms and centimetres. It is not a diagnosis and it does not adjust for a child. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-bmi.s1b: 70 kg and 170 cm is the pair for a BMI of 24.2. The box wants 170, not 1.70 and not a height in feet. 1.70 in the centimetre box is 1.70 cm, and the BMI becomes 242214.5.
calculate-bmi.s2b: The ratio stays in this tab.
calculate-bmi.s3b: Both must be above zero. 70 and 170 become 24.2. The page divides the centimetres by 100 before it squares the metres.
calculate-bmi.s4b: 24.2 is the rounded line. The band is a separate line. Copy keeps both.
calculate-bmi.s5t: Read the band from the cuts
calculate-bmi.s5b: Below 18.5 is Underweight. 18.5 is Normal. 25 is Overweight. 30 is Obesity. 24.2 stays Normal. These are the adult cuts on this page, not a child's chart.
calculate-bmi.s6b: The page only divides two numbers and names a band. It does not see age, muscle, or a clinic. A zero or a negative number fails.
calculate-bmi.diagram2: 18.5 is Normal. 25 is Overweight. 30 is Obesity.

split-tip.name: How to split a tip
split-tip.blurb: 100 at 20% for 4 people is a tip of 20.00, a total of 120.00, and 30.00 each. Each person splits the whole bill. 2.9 people counts as 2.
split-tip.title: How to split a tip
split-tip.lead: You have a bill, a percent, and a number of people. You will read the tip, the total, and the share in this tab. 100 at 20% for 4 people is a tip of 20.00 and 30.00 each. The 30.00 is the whole bill split four ways. The tip alone, split four ways, would be 5.00.
split-tip.result: A tip, a total, and one share, each to two decimals, from one bill, one percent, and one count of people.
split-tip.note: Open the tip split when the bill is zero or more and the people count is at least 1. The page does not name a currency. Nothing is uploaded.
split-tip.s1t: Split the whole bill, not only the tip
split-tip.s1b: 100 at 20% for 4 people: the tip is 20.00, the total is 120.00, and each person pays 30.00. Dividing only the tip by 4 gives 5.00, which is a different question.
split-tip.s2t: Open the tip split on cv.cm
split-tip.s2b: The arithmetic stays in this tab.
split-tip.s3t: Enter the bill, the percent, and the people
split-tip.s3b: The bill must be zero or more. The percent is the tip rate. 100 at 20% adds a tip of 20.00.
split-tip.s4b: All three lines use two decimals. There is no currency. Each is the total divided by the people count the page kept.
split-tip.s5t: A fraction of a person is dropped
split-tip.s5b: 2.9 people counts as 2. On a bill of 100 at 20%, each of those 2 pays 60.00. 1.2 people counts as 1, so the one person pays 120.00.
split-tip.s6b: 0.9 does not become one person, and it does not become zero. The page fails. A bill below zero also fails. A bill of 0 is a tip of 0.00.
split-tip.diagram1: 100 at 20% for 4 people: tip 20.00, total 120.00, each 30.00.
split-tip.diagram2: 2.9 people counts as 2, so each pays 60.00.

loan-payment.name: How to calculate a loan payment
loan-payment.blurb: 10000 at 12% for one year is a monthly payment of 888.49. The interest is 661.85, not 1200. 12000 at 0% for one year is 1000.00 a month.
loan-payment.title: How to calculate a loan payment
loan-payment.lead: You have a principal, an annual percent, and a number of years. You will read the monthly payment, the interest, and the total in this tab. 10000 at 12% for one year is 888.49 a month. The interest is 661.85. A flat 12% of 10000 is 1200, and that is a different sum because this page pays the balance down every month.
loan-payment.result: A monthly payment, the interest, and the total paid, each to two decimals.
loan-payment.note: Open the loan page when the principal is above zero and the years produce at least one month. 12 means 12% a year, not 0.12. Nothing is uploaded.
loan-payment.s1t: Do not multiply the principal by the rate once
loan-payment.s1b: 10000 at 12% for one year is a payment of 888.49 each month, interest of 661.85, and a total of 10661.85. Twelve percent of 10000, taken once, is 1200. The loan interest is lower because each payment reduces the balance.
loan-payment.s2t: Open the loan page on cv.cm
loan-payment.s2b: The schedule stays in this tab. The page does not name a lender.
loan-payment.s3t: Enter principal, annual percent, and years
loan-payment.s3b: 12 in the rate box means 12% a year. The month uses that rate divided by 12. One year is 12 payments. Thirty years is 360 payments. The page rounds years times 12 to a whole number of months.
loan-payment.s4b: All three use two decimals. There is no currency. The payment is the same every month on this page. It is not an amortization table of changing lines.
loan-payment.s5t: A zero rate divides the principal by the months
loan-payment.s5b: 12000 at 0% for one year is a payment of 1000.00, interest of 0.00, and a total of 12000.00. Twelve payments of 1000.00 pay the principal and nothing more.
loan-payment.s6t: A term with no month fails
loan-payment.s6b: The principal must be above zero. Years times 12 is rounded to a whole number of months, and that number must be at least 1. 0.04 years rounds to 0 months and fails.
loan-payment.diagram1: 10000 at 12% for 1 year: payment 888.49, interest 661.85, not 1200.
loan-payment.diagram2: 12000 at 0% for 1 year is 1000.00 a month and 0.00 interest.

read-cron.name: How to read a cron expression
read-cron.blurb: This page reads five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and weekday. 0 9 * * 1 is 09:00 on Monday. Sunday is both 0 and 7. MON and a sixth field fail.
read-cron.title: How to read a cron expression
read-cron.lead: You have a five-field cron expression. You will read what each field names in this tab. The order is minute, hour, day of month, month, weekday. 0 9 * * 1 is minute 0, hour 9, every day of the month, every month, and Monday. The page describes the fields. It does not start the job.
read-cron.result: An English description of the five fields. Weekday 1 is Monday. Weekday 0 and weekday 7 are both Sunday.
read-cron.note: Open cron when the expression is in front of you. Use numbers, stars, commas, and ranges. Words such as MON fail. Nothing is uploaded.
read-cron.s1b: The fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and weekday. 0 9 * * 1 is minute 0, hour 9, every day of the month, every month, and Monday. A star means every value in that field.
read-cron.s2b: The expression stays in this tab.
read-cron.s3b: */15 9-17 * * 1-5 is every 15 minutes, hours 9 through 17, every day of the month, every month, and Monday through Friday. 9-17 includes both 9 and 17. 1-5 is Monday through Friday.
read-cron.s4b: Weekday 1 is Monday. Weekday 0 and weekday 7 both come out as Sunday. The word MON fails. Type 1 for Monday.
read-cron.s5t: Reject a minute of 60 and a sixth field
read-cron.s5b: Minutes run from 0 to 59. Hours run from 0 to 23. Days run from 1 to 31. Months run from 1 to 12. Weekdays run from 0 to 7. 60 * * * * fails. 0 9 * * * * has six fields and fails. There is no seconds field.
read-cron.s6t: Read the description, then leave the job unrun
read-cron.s6b: The line is in English: minute, hour, day-of-month, and names such as monday. When both the day of the month and the weekday are restricted, this page still names both. It does not choose between them, and it does not run anything.
read-cron.diagram1: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, weekday. 0 9 * * 1 is Monday at 09:00.
read-cron.diagram2: Sunday is 0 and 7. MON fails. Six fields fail.

mosaic-photo.name: How to pixelate part of a photo
mosaic-photo.blurb: Black out numbers, pixelate faces, check at 100%, then share.
mosaic-photo.title: How to pixelate part of a photo
mosaic-photo.lead: A photo or screenshot often shows more than you meant to share: a card number, a face, a plate. You will cover them in this tab and check the copy before sending it.
mosaic-photo.result: A copy with the private parts replaced. The original stays on disk.
mosaic-photo.note: This covers areas in your own copy. It cannot undo someone else's mosaic. Nothing is uploaded.
mosaic-photo.s1b: ID and card numbers, QR codes, phone numbers, addresses, plates, and faces of people who did not agree to be shown.
mosaic-photo.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Several photos are fine; each keeps its own boxes.
mosaic-photo.s3b: Keep the original. You are making a copy.
mosaic-photo.s4t: Black box for numbers, mosaic for faces
mosaic-photo.s4b: A fine mosaic can leave digits readable. Use a black box for anything someone could type back in, and make each box a little larger than the text.
mosaic-photo.s5t: Drag a box over each item
mosaic-photo.s5b: Undo removes the last box. For an ID copy, add the for-use-only watermark as well.
mosaic-photo.s6b: Zoom in on every box. If you can still guess a digit, black it out and export again.
mosaic-photo.diagram1: Top: fine mosaic, digits still readable. Middle: coarse mosaic. Bottom: black box, the safe choice for numbers.
mosaic-photo.diagram2: Left: original. Right: the face covered with a coarse mosaic.

watermark-id-copy.name: How to watermark an ID copy before sending it
watermark-id-copy.blurb: Write who it is for, tile it with the date, black out what they do not need.
watermark-id-copy.title: How to watermark an ID copy before sending it
watermark-id-copy.lead: Sending a photo of your ID is sometimes unavoidable. A tiled for-use-only line with a date makes a leaked copy far less useful. You will add it in this tab.
watermark-id-copy.result: An ID copy marked for one receiver, one purpose, and one date.
watermark-id-copy.note: A watermark lowers misuse; it is not a legal guarantee. Some offices still require an unmarked copy, so ask first. Nothing is uploaded.
watermark-id-copy.s1b: Some only need your name and photo. Then you can black out the number and address.
watermark-id-copy.s2b: Work stays in this tab. Front and back can go in together.
watermark-id-copy.s3b: Shoot it flat in even light. Keep the original.
watermark-id-copy.s4t: Press For-use only and name the purpose
watermark-id-copy.s4b: Replace [ORG] with the receiver and purpose, such as “for bank account opening only”. Keep today's date. The line tiles across the whole card, photo included.
watermark-id-copy.s5t: Black out what is not needed
watermark-id-copy.s5b: Open Redact, choose Black box, and drag over the fields they did not ask for.
watermark-id-copy.s6b: The mark should cross the portrait and stay readable while the name is still legible. Export removes EXIF location data.
watermark-id-copy.diagram1: Purpose and date tiled across the whole card; the number is blacked out.
watermark-id-copy.diagram2: Fine mosaic leaves digits readable; a black box does not.

find-bedtime.name: How to find the best bedtime
find-bedtime.blurb: Count back from your alarm in 90-minute cycles plus 14 minutes to fall asleep. A 07:00 alarm means bed at 23:16 for five cycles or 21:46 for six.
find-bedtime.title: How to find the best bedtime
find-bedtime.lead: You have an alarm time. You will find the bedtimes that end a whole sleep cycle, so the alarm rings in light sleep instead of deep sleep. A cycle is about 90 minutes and falling asleep takes about 14 minutes. For a 07:00 alarm, five cycles means lights out at 23:16.
find-bedtime.result: A short list of bedtimes for six, five, four and three cycles, or wake-up times if you start from your bedtime.
find-bedtime.note: Open the sleep calculator when you know your alarm time. Pick five or six cycles on a normal night. The shorter options are for nights when you must. Nothing is uploaded.
find-bedtime.s1b: One cycle is about 90 minutes: light sleep, deep sleep, then REM. Falling asleep takes about 14 minutes. Waking at the end of a cycle feels lighter than waking in the middle of one.
find-bedtime.s2b: Wake-up time is selected and 07:00 is filled. The bedtimes sit on the right. Nothing leaves this tab.
find-bedtime.s3b: Type the time the alarm rings, for example 06:30. Four bedtimes appear: six cycles (9 hours), five (7.5), four (6) and three (4.5). The two longest are marked.
find-bedtime.s4b: For 07:00, six cycles is 21:46 and five is 23:16. Most adults do well on 7.5 to 9 hours. 00:46 (four cycles) and 02:16 (three) are for short nights, not every night.
find-bedtime.s5b: Switch I know my to Bedtime and enter when you lie down, for example 23:00. The list flips to wake-up times: 03:44, 05:14, 06:44 and 08:14. Set the alarm on one of them.
find-bedtime.s6b: If you usually fall asleep in five minutes, go to bed nine minutes later than the list says. If you wake groggy at the suggested time, try the next cycle up or down for a week. Copy puts the list on the clipboard.
find-bedtime.diagram1: Six to three cycles of 90 minutes count back from a 07:00 alarm, each plus 14 minutes to fall asleep.
find-bedtime.diagram2: A 23:00 bedtime plus 14 minutes gives wake-up times at 03:44, 05:14, 06:44 and 08:14.

measure-body-fat.name: How to measure body fat with a tape
measure-body-fat.blurb: Measure neck, waist and hips, enter them with your height, and read the U.S. Navy body fat percentage and its category. Add weight to see fat and lean mass.
measure-body-fat.title: How to measure body fat with a tape
measure-body-fat.lead: You have a tape measure. You will take three or four measurements in centimetres and turn them into a body fat percentage with the U.S. Navy formula. A man of 175 cm with a 38 cm neck and 85 cm waist is about 17%. Nothing leaves this tab.
measure-body-fat.result: A body fat percentage, an ACE category such as fitness or average, and fat and lean mass if you entered weight.
measure-body-fat.note: Open the body fat calculator after measuring. Measure in the morning before eating, with the tape snug but not tight. Repeat the same way to compare over time. Nothing is uploaded.
measure-body-fat.s1b: Neck: just below the larynx, tape sloping slightly down to the front. Waist: at the navel for men, at the narrowest point for women. Hips (women): at the widest point. Read the tape in centimetres, snug but not pressing in.
measure-body-fat.s2t: Open Body fat calculator on cv.cm
measure-body-fat.s2b: Metric and male are selected with sample numbers. The percentage sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
measure-body-fat.s3b: Type your height, neck and waist in centimetres. Switch to imperial for inches. For a woman, pick Female and the hips field appears; the formula needs it.
measure-body-fat.s4t: Add weight if you want mass
measure-body-fat.s4b: Weight is optional. With 70 kg and 17%, fat mass is 11.9 kg and lean mass 58.1 kg. Leave it blank to see only the percentage.
measure-body-fat.s5b: ACE ranges for men: essential 2–5%, athletes 6–13%, fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%, obese 25%+. For women: 10–13%, 14–20%, 21–24%, 25–31%, 32%+.
measure-body-fat.s6t: Compare over time, not with a scan
measure-body-fat.s6b: The tape method is usually within 3 to 4 points of a DEXA scan and less accurate for very lean or very muscular people. Measure the same way every few weeks and watch the trend. Copy puts the result on the clipboard.
measure-body-fat.diagram1: Tape positions: neck below the larynx, waist at the navel (men) or narrowest point (women), hips at the widest point.
measure-body-fat.diagram2: 175 cm, 38 cm neck, 85 cm waist: about 17%, in the fitness band for men.

check-contrast.name: How to check color contrast for WCAG
check-contrast.blurb: Enter the text and background hex colors and read the ratio. Normal text needs 4.5:1 for AA and 7:1 for AAA; large text needs 3:1 and 4.5:1. A passing color is suggested.
check-contrast.title: How to check color contrast for WCAG
check-contrast.lead: You have a text color and a background color. You will read their contrast ratio and see whether the pair passes WCAG 2 AA and AAA. Grey #777777 on white is 4.48:1 and fails AA for normal text by a hair; #767676 passes. Nothing leaves this tab.
check-contrast.result: A ratio such as 4.48:1, pass or fail for AA and AAA at normal and large sizes, and the closest text color that passes when the pair fails.
check-contrast.note: Open the contrast checker with both hex codes at hand. Check body text against 4.5:1, headings over 24px against 3:1, and icons or borders against 3:1. Nothing is uploaded.
check-contrast.s1b: WCAG 2 AA: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. AAA: 7:1 and 4.5:1. Large text is 24px regular or about 18.7px bold. Icons, borders and form controls need 3:1.
check-contrast.s2b: A sample pink on cream pair is filled. The ratio and the pass/fail rows sit on the right under a text sample. Nothing is uploaded.
check-contrast.s3b: Type a hex code such as #777777 for text and #ffffff for background, or pick with the color swatch. Three-digit codes like #777 work too. The sample updates as you type.
check-contrast.s4t: Read the ratio and the rows
check-contrast.s4b: #777777 on #ffffff is 4.48:1: AA large text and UI pass, AA normal text fails. Each row says Pass or Fail against its threshold.
check-contrast.s5b: When normal text fails AA, the page suggests the closest text color that reaches 4.5:1, moving toward black or white. For #777777 on white it suggests #767676. Swap exchanges text and background.
check-contrast.s6b: Repeat for links, hover and disabled colors, and for text on images use the darkest part of the image as background. Copy puts the colors, ratio and results on the clipboard.
check-contrast.diagram1: Ratio thresholds: 3:1 for large text and UI, 4.5:1 for AA normal text, 7:1 for AAA normal text.
check-contrast.diagram2: #777777 on white is 4.48:1 and fails AA normal text; #767676 reaches 4.54:1 and passes.

calculate-pace.name: How to calculate running pace
calculate-pace.blurb: Enter distance and time to get pace per km and per mile, or enter pace to get a finish time. 10 km in 55:00 is 5:30 /km, 8:51 /mi, and a 3:52:04 marathon at the same pace.
calculate-pace.title: How to calculate running pace
calculate-pace.lead: You ran a distance in a time, or you want to finish in a time. You will turn that into pace per kilometre and per mile, and see what the same pace gives for 5K, 10K, half and marathon. 10 km in 55:00 is 5:30 /km. Nothing leaves this tab.
calculate-pace.result: Pace per km and per mile, speed, and finish times for the four common races at the same pace.
calculate-pace.note: Open the pace calculator with the numbers from your watch or race plan. Type time as h:mm:ss or mm:ss and pace as m:ss. Race predictions assume an even pace. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-pace.s1t: Pick what you want to find
calculate-pace.s1b: Pace = time ÷ distance. Time = pace × distance. Distance = time ÷ pace. Decide which one you are missing; you fill in the other two.
calculate-pace.s2b: Pace is selected with 10 km in 55:00. The result and race times sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-pace.s3b: Type 10 for distance and 55:00 for time. The pace reads 05:30 per km and 08:51 per mile, and the speed 10.91 km/h. Switch Unit to mi for miles.
calculate-pace.s4t: Or enter pace to get a time
calculate-pace.s4b: Set Calculate to Time, type the distance and a pace such as 5:00. A half marathon at 5:00 /km finishes in 1:45:29.
calculate-pace.s5b: At 5:30 /km: 5K 27:30, 10K 55:00, half 1:56:02, marathon 3:52:04. Real races slow over distance, so plan a longer race a little slower than a short one.
calculate-pace.s6b: Copy puts distance, time, both paces, speed and the four race times on the clipboard for a training log.
calculate-pace.diagram1: Pace = time ÷ distance: 55:00 over 10 km is 5:30 per km or 8:51 per mile.

calculate-final-grade.name: How to calculate the grade you need on a final
calculate-final-grade.blurb: Enter your current grade, the grade you want and the final's weight. 85% now, 90% wanted and a 30% final needs 101.7%, so aim for a B instead. Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight.
calculate-final-grade.title: How to calculate the grade you need on a final
calculate-final-grade.lead: You know your grade so far, the grade you want and how much the final counts. You will find the score the final must reach. With 85% now, a 90% goal and a 30% final, you need 101.7%, which means an A is out of reach but a B needs only 68.3%. Nothing leaves this tab.
calculate-final-grade.result: The score needed on the final, a note when it is over 100% or already reached, and a table for A, B, C and D.
calculate-final-grade.note: Open the final grade calculator with the syllabus at hand for the final's weight. Use your current weighted average as the current grade. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-final-grade.s1b: Current grade: your average so far, as a percentage. Grade you want: the target for the course. Weight of the final: from the syllabus, such as 30%. The rest of the course is then 70%.
calculate-final-grade.s2t: Open Final grade calculator on cv.cm
calculate-final-grade.s2b: 85%, 90% and a 30% final are filled. The needed score sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-final-grade.s3b: Type the current grade, the wanted grade and the weight. The needed score updates as you type: with 85, 90 and 30 it reads 101.7% on the final.
calculate-final-grade.s4b: Over 100% means the goal cannot be reached on the final alone without extra credit. Look at the letter table: a B (80%) needs 68.3%, a C needs 35%.
calculate-final-grade.s5t: Read a result at 0% or below
calculate-final-grade.s5b: With 95% now, 90% wanted and a 20% final, the needed score is 70%. If the result is 0% or less, you already have the grade and any score keeps it.
calculate-final-grade.s6b: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. For 90, 85 and 0.30: (90 − 59.5) ÷ 0.30 = 101.7. Copy puts the result and the table on the clipboard.
calculate-final-grade.diagram1: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight. 85% now, 90% wanted, 30% final: 101.7%.
calculate-final-grade.diagram2: Same numbers per letter: A needs 101.7%, B 68.3%, C 35%, D 1.7%.

calculate-tdee.name: How to calculate TDEE and daily calories
calculate-tdee.blurb: Enter sex, age, weight, height and activity. BMR comes from Mifflin–St Jeor and TDEE is BMR times an activity factor. A 30-year-old man, 70 kg, 175 cm, moderate activity: 1649 and 2556 kcal.
calculate-tdee.title: How to calculate TDEE and daily calories
calculate-tdee.lead: You want to know how many calories you burn in a day. You will enter five numbers and read BMR (at rest) and TDEE (with activity), plus a cut and a bulk target. A 30-year-old man of 70 kg and 175 cm with moderate activity burns about 2556 kcal a day. Nothing leaves this tab.
calculate-tdee.result: BMR, TDEE, a weight-loss target 500 kcal below and a gain target 300 kcal above, with a floor for safe cutting.
calculate-tdee.note: Open the TDEE calculator with your weight and height at hand. Pick the activity level honestly; most desk workers who train three times a week are light or moderate. An estimate, not medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-tdee.s1b: BMR is the energy you burn at complete rest. TDEE multiplies it by an activity factor from 1.2 (sedentary) to 1.9 (training twice a day). Eat at TDEE to hold weight.
calculate-tdee.s2b: Metric, male, 30 years, 70 kg, 175 cm and moderate are filled. The calories sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-tdee.s3b: Pick sex, type age, weight and height. Switch to imperial for pounds, feet and inches; the numbers convert as you switch. Age 15 to 100 is accepted.
calculate-tdee.s4b: Sedentary 1.2: desk job, little exercise. Light 1.375: 1–3 days a week. Moderate 1.55: 3–5 days. Active 1.725: hard exercise 6–7 days. Very active 1.9: physical job or two sessions a day.
calculate-tdee.s5b: For the sample man: BMR 1649, maintain 2556, lose 2056 (−500 kcal, about 0.5 kg a week), gain 2856 (+300 kcal). The cut never goes below 1500 kcal for men or 1200 for women; a note says when it was raised.
calculate-tdee.s6b: Weigh yourself weekly. If weight does not move at the cut target after four weeks, choose the next lower activity level and recalculate. Copy puts the four numbers on the clipboard.
calculate-tdee.diagram1: BMR from Mifflin–St Jeor, TDEE = BMR × activity factor 1.2 to 1.9.
calculate-tdee.diagram2: Sample man: maintain 2556, lose 2056 (−500), gain 2856 (+300) kcal a day.

calculate-gpa.name: How to calculate GPA on the 4.0 scale
calculate-gpa.blurb: Enter a letter grade and credits per course. Each grade becomes points (A 4.0, B+ 3.3, B 3.0), points times credits are added and divided by total credits. A 3, B+ 3, A- 4, B 3 gives 3.51.
calculate-gpa.title: How to calculate GPA on the 4.0 scale
calculate-gpa.lead: You have letter grades and credits for the term. You will turn them into a credit-weighted GPA on the 4.0 scale. Four courses, A (3 credits), B+ (3), A- (4) and B (3), give 45.7 points over 13 credits, a GPA of 3.51. Nothing leaves this tab.
calculate-gpa.result: A GPA to two decimals, total credits, quality points and the number of courses counted.
calculate-gpa.note: Open the GPA calculator with your transcript at hand. Pass/fail courses do not count. If your school gives A+ 4.3, tick the box. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-gpa.s2b: Four sample courses are filled. GPA, credits and quality points sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-gpa.s3b: Pick the letter grade and type the credits in each row. Add course adds a row; × removes one. Credits above 30 or 0 are skipped as typos.
calculate-gpa.s4b: A × 3 = 12, B+ × 3 = 9.9, A- × 4 = 14.8, B × 3 = 9. Total 45.7 points over 13 credits = 3.51. Quality points and total credits are shown so you can check.
calculate-gpa.s5b: Tick A+ = 4.3 only if your school uses it; the GPA can then exceed 4.0. Leave pass/fail courses out; they usually add credits but no points.
calculate-gpa.s6b: Copy puts the GPA, total credits, quality points and course count on the clipboard. For a cumulative GPA, add every term's courses in one list.
calculate-gpa.diagram1: Letter to points: A 4.0, A- 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, C 2.0, D 1.0, F 0.
calculate-gpa.diagram2: A 3, B+ 3, A- 4, B 3: 45.7 points over 13 credits = 3.51.

use-pomodoro.name: How to use a Pomodoro timer
use-pomodoro.blurb: Start a 25-minute focus block, rest 5 minutes at the chime, and take a 15-minute break after four rounds. The tab title shows the time left; the chime needs the tab open.
use-pomodoro.title: How to use a Pomodoro timer
use-pomodoro.lead: You have a task that keeps slipping. You will work in 25-minute blocks with 5-minute breaks and a 15-minute break after four. The timer counts from the clock, chimes at each change and moves to the next phase by itself. Nothing leaves this tab.
use-pomodoro.result: A running countdown in the page and the tab title, a chime at each change, and a count of finished focus blocks.
use-pomodoro.note: Open the Pomodoro timer before you start the task, not during it. Write one task per block. Keep the tab open for the chime. Nothing is uploaded.
use-pomodoro.s1b: Write down the one thing for the next 25 minutes. Close chat and mail. A block that gets interrupted does not count; start it again.
use-pomodoro.s2b: 25-minute focus, 5-minute short break, 15-minute long break and 4 rounds are set. Nothing is uploaded.
use-pomodoro.s3b: The clock counts down and the tab title shows the time left, so you can switch tabs. At 00:00 a chime plays and the break starts by itself.
use-pomodoro.s4b: Stand up, drink water, do not open the task. After the 5-minute break the next focus block starts on its own. After four blocks the break is 15 minutes.
use-pomodoro.s5b: Pause stops the clock without losing time. Skip jumps to the next phase; a skipped focus block does not count toward the long break. Reset starts over from round 1.
use-pomodoro.s6b: While stopped, set focus, short break and long break from 1 to 180 minutes and rounds from 1 to 12. 50/10 suits deep work; 15/3 suits chores. The current phase takes the new length right away.
use-pomodoro.diagram1: Four 25-minute focus blocks with 5-minute breaks, then a 15-minute long break.
use-pomodoro.diagram2: Pause keeps the time left; Skip moves on without counting the block; Reset starts at round 1.

find-due-date.name: How to calculate a due date
find-due-date.blurb: Enter the first day of the last period and the cycle length. Due date = last period + 280 days, shifted by cycle − 28. A period starting 1 January gives 8 October; a 32-day cycle gives 12 October.
find-due-date.title: How to calculate a due date
find-due-date.lead: You know the first day of the last period, or the conception date, or a due date from a scan. You will turn it into the due date, the week of pregnancy today and the trimester dates. A period starting 1 January with a 28-day cycle gives a due date of 8 October. Nothing leaves this tab.
find-due-date.result: The due date, weeks and days pregnant today, the trimester, days left, the estimated conception date and the dates the second and third trimesters start.
find-due-date.note: Open the due date calculator with the date of the last period at hand. Use the cycle length from a period app if you have one. An estimate, not medical advice; an early ultrasound overrides it. Nothing is uploaded.
find-due-date.s1b: Pregnancy is counted from the first day of the last period, not from conception. Due date = that day + 280 days (40 weeks) for a 28-day cycle. A longer cycle ovulates later, so each extra day moves the due date a day later.
find-due-date.s2t: Open Due date calculator on cv.cm
find-due-date.s2b: Last period is selected with a sample date and a 28-day cycle. The due date and today's week sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
find-due-date.s3t: Enter the last period and cycle length
find-due-date.s3b: Type the first day of the last period, for example 1 January. Leave 28 days or change it: 32 days moves the due date from 8 October to 12 October.
find-due-date.s4b: On 12 March that pregnancy is 10 weeks 0 days, first trimester, 210 days to go. The second trimester starts at 13 weeks (2 April), the third at 27 weeks (9 July).
find-due-date.s5t: Or start from conception or a known due date
find-due-date.s5b: Switch I know my to Conception date (due date is 266 days later) or to Due date from a scan. The weeks, trimesters and other dates follow from it.
find-due-date.s6t: Treat it as a window, then copy
find-due-date.s6b: Only about 4 in 100 babies arrive on the due date; most come within two weeks either side. Copy puts the dates on the clipboard for the first appointment.
find-due-date.diagram1: Count from the first day of the last period: 280 days for a 28-day cycle, plus one day per extra cycle day.
find-due-date.diagram2: Last period 1 January: conception about 15 January, second trimester 2 April, third 9 July, due 8 October.

find-ideal-weight.name: How to find your ideal weight
find-ideal-weight.blurb: Enter sex and height to read the Devine, Robinson, Miller and Hamwi ideal weights and the BMI 18.5–24.9 range. A 170 cm man: 65.9 kg Devine, 65.2 kg Robinson, 66 kg Miller, 66.7 kg Hamwi, BMI range 53.5–72 kg.
find-ideal-weight.title: How to find your ideal weight
find-ideal-weight.lead: You want a sensible weight target for your height. You will read four classic formulas and the healthy BMI range in one place, in kilograms or pounds. For a 170 cm man the formulas land between 65.2 and 66.7 kg and the BMI range is 53.5 to 72 kg. Nothing leaves this tab.
find-ideal-weight.result: Four ideal weights (Devine, Robinson, Miller, Hamwi) and the weight range for a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 at your height.
find-ideal-weight.note: Open the ideal weight calculator with your height at hand. Read the spread of the formulas as the range, and the BMI row as the healthy band. Not a personal target; ask a doctor. Nothing is uploaded.
find-ideal-weight.s1b: Devine (1974), Robinson (1983), Miller (1983) and Hamwi (1964) each give a base weight at 5 feet and add a fixed amount per inch above it, with separate numbers for men and women. They were built for drug dosing and insurance tables, so they differ by a few kilograms.
find-ideal-weight.s2t: Open Ideal weight calculator on cv.cm
find-ideal-weight.s2b: Metric, male and 170 cm are set. The four results and the BMI range sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
find-ideal-weight.s3b: Pick Male or Female and type the height in cm. For feet and inches switch Units to imperial; the results then show in pounds. Below 5 ft (152.4 cm) the formulas extrapolate, so treat those results as rough.
find-ideal-weight.s4b: For a 170 cm man: Devine 65.9 kg, Robinson 65.2 kg, Miller 66 kg, Hamwi 66.7 kg. For a 160 cm woman: 52.4, 54.1, 57.2 and 52.1 kg. The spread is the answer; no single formula is right.
find-ideal-weight.s5b: The last row is the weight that gives a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9: 53.5 to 72 kg at 170 cm. Muscle, frame and age shift what is healthy for you.
find-ideal-weight.s6b: Copy puts the five lines on the clipboard. For calories to reach a target, open the TDEE calculator next.
find-ideal-weight.diagram1: Each formula: a base weight at 5 ft plus a fixed amount per inch, different for men and women.
find-ideal-weight.diagram2: 170 cm man: Devine 65.9, Robinson 65.2, Miller 66, Hamwi 66.7 kg; BMI range 53.5–72 kg.

daily-water.name: How to work out how much water to drink a day
daily-water.blurb: 35 ml per kg of body weight, plus 12 ml per minute of exercise, plus 500 ml in hot weather. 70 kg with 30 minutes of exercise gives about 2.8 litres, 12 glasses of 250 ml.
daily-water.title: How to work out how much water to drink a day
daily-water.lead: You want a daily water target that fits your body and your day, not a flat eight glasses. You will enter weight, exercise minutes and climate and read litres and glasses. A 70 kg person with 30 minutes of exercise in a temperate climate gets about 2.8 litres. Nothing leaves this tab.
daily-water.result: Total water a day in litres and 250 ml glasses, split into the part from body weight, from exercise and from climate.
daily-water.note: Open the water intake calculator with your weight at hand. Count tea, coffee, milk and food toward the total. A rule of thumb for healthy adults, not medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
daily-water.s1b: About 35 ml per kilogram of body weight a day covers a healthy adult at rest in mild weather. Exercise adds roughly 12 ml per minute (360 ml per half hour). Hot or humid weather adds about half a litre.
daily-water.s2t: Open Water intake calculator on cv.cm
daily-water.s2b: 70 kg, 30 minutes of exercise and a temperate climate are set. The total sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
daily-water.s3b: Type the weight in kg, or switch the unit to lb. 70 kg gives a base of 2450 ml; 60 kg gives 2100 ml.
daily-water.s4b: Enter the minutes of exercise on a typical day. 30 minutes adds 360 ml; an hour adds 720 ml. Use 0 on rest days.
daily-water.s5b: Pick Hot or humid in summer or in the tropics to add 500 ml. For 70 kg, 30 minutes and hot weather the total is 3.31 litres, 14 glasses.
daily-water.s6t: Spread it through the day, then copy
daily-water.s6b: 12 glasses is one every hour or so while awake; thirst and pale urine are the simple checks. Copy puts the breakdown on the clipboard.
daily-water.diagram1: 35 ml × kg, plus 12 ml × exercise minutes, plus 500 ml in heat.
daily-water.diagram2: 70 kg and 30 minutes: 2450 + 360 = 2810 ml, about 12 glasses of 250 ml.

trip-fuel-cost.name: How to calculate the fuel cost of a trip
trip-fuel-cost.blurb: Distance × economy gives litres, litres × price gives cost. 300 km at 7 L/100 km uses 21 litres; at 1.60 a litre that is 33.60, or 67.20 for the round trip, 22.40 each for three people.
trip-fuel-cost.title: How to calculate the fuel cost of a trip
trip-fuel-cost.lead: You are planning a drive and want the fuel bill before you leave. You will enter distance, your car's economy and the pump price, then read litres, cost, cost per person and cost per 100 km. 300 km at 7 L/100 km and 1.60 a litre costs 33.60. Nothing leaves this tab.
trip-fuel-cost.result: Total cost, litres used, cost per person, cost per 100 km and the distance driven, in whatever currency you type.
trip-fuel-cost.note: Open the fuel cost calculator with the route distance and your car's economy at hand. Use the combined figure from the dashboard trip computer. Add about 10% for city traffic or a loaded car. Nothing is uploaded.
trip-fuel-cost.s1b: Distance from the map app. Economy from the car's trip computer or the spec sheet: L/100 km in most countries, km/L in some, mpg in the US. Price from the last fill-up, per litre or per gallon.
trip-fuel-cost.s2t: Open Fuel cost calculator on cv.cm
trip-fuel-cost.s2b: 300 km at 7 L/100 km and 1.60 per litre are set. The cost sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
trip-fuel-cost.s3b: Type the distance and pick km or mi. Type the economy and pick L/100 km, km/L or mpg. Type the price and pick per litre or per US gallon. The tool converts between them.
trip-fuel-cost.s4b: 300 km at 7 L/100 km uses 21 litres; at 1.60 that is 33.60, or 11.20 per 100 km. In US units, 100 miles at 30 mpg and 3.50 a gallon is 11.67.
trip-fuel-cost.s5b: Tick Round trip to double the distance: 67.20. Set People sharing to 3 and each pays 22.40, driver included.
trip-fuel-cost.s6b: Economy figures are for mixed driving; stop-and-go traffic, air conditioning and a full boot use about 10% more. Copy puts the result on the clipboard.
trip-fuel-cost.diagram1: Litres = distance ÷ 100 × L/100 km; cost = litres × price per litre.
trip-fuel-cost.diagram2: 300 km, 7 L/100 km, 1.60: 21 L and 33.60; round trip 67.20; three people 22.40 each.

estimate-reading-time.name: How to estimate reading time for a text
estimate-reading-time.blurb: Paste the text. Words ÷ 238 gives silent reading minutes, words ÷ 130 gives speaking minutes. 650 words is a five-minute talk; 1200 words is a five-minute read. Chinese, Japanese and Korean are counted in characters.
estimate-reading-time.title: How to estimate reading time for a text
estimate-reading-time.lead: You have an article to label, a post to size or a speech to time. You will paste the text and read how long it takes to read silently at three speeds and to read aloud. A 1200-word article is about five minutes; a 650-word speech is about five minutes aloud. Nothing leaves this tab.
estimate-reading-time.result: Reading time and speaking time, plus words (or CJK characters), characters, and characters without spaces.
estimate-reading-time.note: Open the reading time calculator with the final draft. Use Average for articles, Slow for technical text, and the speaking row for talks and videos. Nothing is uploaded.
estimate-reading-time.s1b: Adults read non-fiction silently at about 238 words a minute (Brysbaert, 2019); 150 is slow or technical, 300 is fast. Speaking runs near 130 words a minute. Chinese, Japanese and Korean are counted in characters at 300 a minute.
estimate-reading-time.s2t: Open Reading time calculator on cv.cm
estimate-reading-time.s2b: A sample paragraph is filled at average speed. The times and counts sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
estimate-reading-time.s3b: Press Clear and paste the article, essay or script. 1200 words reads as 5 min 3 s at average speed and 9 min 14 s aloud.
estimate-reading-time.s4b: Choose Slow for manuals and legal text, Fast for light reading. Speaking time does not change with the speed setting.
estimate-reading-time.s5b: For a five-minute talk aim for about 650 words; for a 60-second video about 130. Presenters vary from 110 to 150 words a minute, so allow a minute for pauses.
estimate-reading-time.s6b: Copy puts the times and counts on the clipboard for a byline such as "5 min read". Word count and character count are also on the right.
estimate-reading-time.diagram1: Reading minutes = words ÷ 238; speaking minutes = words ÷ 130; CJK uses characters ÷ 300.
estimate-reading-time.diagram2: 1200 words: about 5 minutes to read, 9 minutes aloud. 650 words: a five-minute talk.

compare-text.name: How to compare two texts and see the differences
compare-text.blurb: Paste the original on the left and the new version on the right. Added lines show green, removed lines red, and the counts sit above. Tick Ignore extra spaces to skip whitespace changes; copy a unified diff for a ticket.
compare-text.title: How to compare two texts and see the differences
compare-text.lead: You have two versions of a document, a config or a contract clause and need to see what changed. You will paste both and read the added and removed lines, with a count of each. Nothing leaves this tab.
compare-text.result: A line-by-line diff: removed lines marked −, added lines marked +, unchanged lines plain, with +/− counts and a unified diff you can copy.
compare-text.note: Open the diff checker with both versions at hand. Put the older text on the left so added lines read as new. Nothing is uploaded.
compare-text.s1b: The left box is the original and the right box is the changed version. Lines only on the right show as added (+), lines only on the left as removed (−). Swapping them flips the colors.
compare-text.s2b: Two empty boxes and the result area are ready. Nothing is uploaded.
compare-text.s3b: Paste the original on the left and the new version on the right. The diff appears as you paste; the line above it counts added, removed and unchanged lines.
compare-text.s4t: Ignore whitespace when it is noise
compare-text.s4b: Tick Ignore extra spaces when an editor re-indented the text or changed tabs to spaces; only real content changes then show.
compare-text.s5b: Each changed line is shown once as − (old) and once as + (new). A line that moved shows as removed in one place and added in another; a diff does not track moves.
compare-text.s6b: Copy unified diff puts the standard patch format on the clipboard, with --- and +++ headers and @@ hunks, ready for a ticket, a code review or `patch`.
compare-text.diagram1: Original on the left, changed text on the right: − lines are removed, + lines are added.
compare-text.diagram2: Ignore extra spaces hides re-indenting and tab changes so only content changes show.

hash-text.name: How to get the MD5 or SHA-256 hash of text or a file
hash-text.blurb: Pick MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, paste text or choose a file, and copy the hex or Base64 digest. Compare it with the checksum a download page lists; one different character means a different file.
hash-text.title: How to get the MD5 or SHA-256 hash of text or a file
hash-text.lead: You downloaded a file and the site lists a SHA-256 checksum, or you need the MD5 of a string for a config. You will hash the text or file in this tab and compare the digest. The SHA-256 of an empty string starts e3b0c442. Nothing leaves this tab.
hash-text.result: The digest in hex and Base64 for the chosen algorithm, for text as you type or for a local file.
hash-text.note: Open the hash generator with the expected checksum at hand. Use SHA-256 to verify downloads; MD5 and SHA-1 only when the other side requires them. Nothing is uploaded.
hash-text.s1t: Pick the algorithm the other side uses
hash-text.s1b: A checksum must be compared with the same algorithm. Download pages usually give SHA-256 (64 hex characters); older ones give MD5 (32) or SHA-1 (40). SHA-384 and SHA-512 are longer. MD5 and SHA-1 are fine for integrity checks but not for security.
hash-text.s2b: SHA-256 is selected and the text box is empty. Nothing is uploaded.
hash-text.s3b: Type or paste the text. The hex digest updates as you type, and Base64 sits below it. Trailing spaces and line breaks change the hash, so paste exactly.
hash-text.s4b: Press Hash a file and pick the download. The file is read in this tab and the digest appears with the file name; large files take a few seconds.
hash-text.s5b: Read the digest against the published checksum: compare the first and last eight characters, then the whole string if they match. Any difference means the file is not the one published: download it again.
hash-text.s6b: Copy hex puts the digest on the clipboard in lower case. Hashes are case-insensitive in hex, so ABCD and abcd match.
hash-text.diagram1: Same algorithm on both sides: SHA-256 gives 64 hex characters, MD5 32, SHA-1 40.
hash-text.diagram2: Compare the digest with the published checksum; one different character means a different file.

generate-uuid.name: How to generate a UUID
generate-uuid.blurb: Set how many, choose hyphens and case, press Generate and copy the list. Each UUID is version 4, 122 random bits from Web Crypto, such as 3f2504e0-4f89-41d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301.
generate-uuid.title: How to generate a UUID
generate-uuid.lead: You need a unique id for a record, a test fixture or an API key placeholder. You will generate one or many random UUIDs in this tab and copy them. A version 4 UUID looks like 3f2504e0-4f89-41d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301. Nothing leaves this tab.
generate-uuid.result: A list of random version 4 UUIDs, with or without hyphens, in lower or upper case, ready to copy.
generate-uuid.note: Open the UUID generator when you need ids. The values are random and never stored; generate again for a fresh set. Nothing is uploaded.
generate-uuid.s1t: Know what a UUID v4 is
generate-uuid.s1b: 36 characters: 32 hex digits in groups of 8-4-4-4-12. The third group starts with 4 (version) and the fourth with 8, 9, a or b (variant). The other 122 bits are random, so collisions are not a practical concern.
generate-uuid.s2b: Five UUIDs with hyphens in lower case are ready; the list refreshes as you change the options. Nothing is uploaded.
generate-uuid.s3b: Drag the How many slider from 1 to 20. The list updates at once, one UUID per line; press Generate for a fresh set with the same settings.
generate-uuid.s4b: Untick Hyphens for a 32-character form some databases and file names want. Tick Uppercase if a schema or Windows registry key expects capitals. Both forms are the same UUID.
generate-uuid.s5b: Copy list puts every UUID on the clipboard, one per line, for a SQL insert, a fixture file or a spreadsheet column.
generate-uuid.s6b: v4 is random and right for most ids. If you need ids that sort by time, use UUID v7 or a ULID from your database or language instead.
generate-uuid.diagram1: 8-4-4-4-12 hex groups; the third group starts with 4, the fourth with 8, 9, a or b.
generate-uuid.diagram2: Hyphens off gives 32 characters; Uppercase gives capitals; both name the same UUID.

calculate-work-hours.name: How to calculate hours worked on a time card
calculate-work-hours.blurb: Enter start, end and unpaid break for each shift. 09:00–17:30 with 30 minutes off is 8 hours, five days is 40, and a Saturday 09:00–14:00 adds 5 hours of overtime: 950.00 at 20 an hour with 1.5× overtime.
calculate-work-hours.title: How to calculate hours worked on a time card
calculate-work-hours.lead: You have a week of clock-in and clock-out times and want the hours, the overtime and the pay. You will enter each shift once and read the totals. Five shifts of 09:00–17:30 with a 30-minute break are 40 hours; a Saturday morning on top makes 45, with 5 hours of overtime. Nothing leaves this tab.
calculate-work-hours.result: Hours per shift, the week's total in hours:minutes and decimal hours, regular and overtime hours, and gross pay if you entered a rate.
calculate-work-hours.note: Open the time card calculator with your shift times at hand. Enter unpaid breaks only; paid breaks count as work. Overtime rules differ by country and contract, so set the threshold and multiplier to match yours. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-work-hours.s1b: For each day you need the clock-in time, the clock-out time and the unpaid break in minutes. One shift = end − start − break: 09:00 to 17:30 is 8 hours 30 minutes, minus 30 minutes is 8 hours.
calculate-work-hours.s2t: Open Time card calculator on cv.cm
calculate-work-hours.s2b: Five shifts of 09:00–17:30 with 30-minute breaks are filled: 40:00 hours. Each row shows its hours on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-work-hours.s3b: Change the start, end and break per row. Add shift adds a sixth day; × removes a row. A row marked ! has a missing time or a break longer than the shift.
calculate-work-hours.s4b: If the end time is earlier than the start, the shift runs past midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours and shows a ☾. Do not split it into two days.
calculate-work-hours.s5b: Add Saturday 09:00–14:00 with no break: total 45:00, regular 40:00, overtime 5:00. With a rate of 20 and the default 1.5×, gross pay is 800 + 150 = 950.00.
calculate-work-hours.s6t: Convert to decimal hours and copy
calculate-work-hours.s6b: Payroll often wants decimal hours: divide minutes by 60, so 7:45 is 7.75. The totals show both forms. Copy puts them on the clipboard.
calculate-work-hours.diagram1: One shift = end − start − unpaid break: 09:00–17:30 minus 30 minutes is 8 hours.
calculate-work-hours.diagram2: 45 hours in a week with a 40-hour threshold: 40 regular + 5 overtime at 1.5×.

electricity-cost.name: How to calculate the electricity cost of an appliance
electricity-cost.blurb: Watts × hours ÷ 1000 = kWh; kWh × your price = cost. A 1000 W air conditioner for 8 hours a day for 30 days uses 240 kWh: 36.00 at 0.15 a kWh, 438.00 a year.
electricity-cost.title: How to calculate the electricity cost of an appliance
electricity-cost.lead: You want to know what an appliance adds to the bill. You will read its watts, estimate how long it runs and multiply by your price per kWh. A 1000 W air conditioner running 8 hours a day for a month uses 240 kWh; at 0.15 that is 36.00. Nothing leaves this tab.
electricity-cost.result: Cost for the period, energy in kWh, cost and kWh per day, and cost per year, in whatever currency you type.
electricity-cost.note: Open the electricity cost calculator with the appliance label and your latest bill at hand. Fridges and air conditioners cycle on and off, so their real use is lower than the label. Nothing is uploaded.
electricity-cost.s1b: Energy in kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Cost = kWh × price per kWh. A 1000 W heater running one hour uses exactly 1 kWh.
electricity-cost.s2t: Open Electricity cost calculator on cv.cm
electricity-cost.s2b: A 1000 W air conditioner, 8 hours a day, 30 days at 0.15 per kWh is filled. The cost sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
electricity-cost.s3b: Pick a preset or type the watts from the label or manual. If the label gives amps, multiply by the voltage: 5 A × 220 V = 1100 W.
electricity-cost.s4b: Type the hours a day it runs and the number of days. Take the price per kWh from your bill: energy charge ÷ kWh used. For several identical devices set How many.
electricity-cost.s5b: The air conditioner: 240 kWh, 36.00 for the month, 1.20 a day, 438.00 a year. A 10 W LED bulb for 5 hours a day uses 1.5 kWh a month: 0.30 at 0.20 a kWh.
electricity-cost.s6t: Account for cycling and standby, then copy
electricity-cost.s6b: A 150 W fridge on 24 hours shows 3.6 kWh a day, but the compressor runs about a third of the time, so expect nearer 1.2. Standby of a few watts all year adds up to tens of kWh. Copy puts the numbers on the clipboard.
electricity-cost.diagram1: kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000; cost = kWh × price per kWh.
electricity-cost.diagram2: 1000 W × 8 h × 30 days = 240 kWh; at 0.15 that is 36.00 a month.

find-fertile-window.name: How to find your fertile window and ovulation day
find-fertile-window.blurb: Ovulation is about 14 days before the next period. A period starting 1 January with a 28-day cycle gives ovulation on 15 January, a fertile window of 10–15 January and the next period on 29 January.
find-fertile-window.title: How to find your fertile window and ovulation day
find-fertile-window.lead: You know when your last period started and roughly how long your cycle is. You will find the likely ovulation day, the six-day fertile window and the next period for the next three cycles. With a 1 January start and 28 days, ovulation falls on 15 January. Nothing leaves this tab.
find-fertile-window.result: For each of the next three cycles: the fertile window, the likely ovulation day and the next period.
find-fertile-window.note: Open the ovulation calculator with your period dates at hand. Use the average of your last few cycles. It is an estimate, not contraception or medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
find-fertile-window.s1b: The time from ovulation to the next period, the luteal phase, is about 14 days for most people. The part before ovulation is what varies, so ovulation = next period − 14 days.
find-fertile-window.s2b: A sample last period and a 28-day cycle are filled. Three cycles sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
find-fertile-window.s3b: Type the first day of your last period, the first day of bleeding. For 1 January with 28 days, the next period is 29 January.
find-fertile-window.s4b: Count from the first day of one period to the day before the next and average a few cycles. A 32-day cycle moves ovulation from 15 January to 19 January.
find-fertile-window.s5b: The window is the five days before ovulation plus ovulation day: 10–15 January. Sperm can live up to five days and the egg about one, so these six days carry the highest chance.
find-fertile-window.s6t: Treat it as an estimate, then copy
find-fertile-window.s6b: Cycles shift by a few days from month to month, and calendar estimates miss many ovulations. Ovulation test strips give a better signal. Copy puts the dates on the clipboard.
find-fertile-window.diagram1: Ovulation ≈ next period − 14 days; the fertile window runs from 5 days before through ovulation day.
find-fertile-window.diagram2: Period 1 January, 28 days: fertile 10–15 January, ovulation 15 January, next period 29 January.

calculate-macros.name: How to calculate your macros in grams
calculate-macros.blurb: Split a calorie target into protein, fat and carbs. Grams = calories × share ÷ 4 for protein and carbs, ÷ 9 for fat. 2500 kcal at 30/30/40 is 188 g protein, 83 g fat and 250 g carbs.
calculate-macros.title: How to calculate your macros in grams
calculate-macros.lead: You know roughly how many calories you need and want to turn that into grams on a food label. You will pick a goal and a split and read protein, fat and carbohydrate in grams. 2500 kcal with a balanced 30/30/40 split is 188 g protein, 83 g fat and 250 g carbs. Nothing leaves this tab.
calculate-macros.result: A daily calorie target and grams of protein, fat and carbohydrate, plus protein per kg if you entered your weight.
calculate-macros.note: Open the macro calculator with your maintenance calories at hand; the TDEE calculator estimates them. A starting point for healthy adults, not medical advice. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-macros.s1b: Protein and carbohydrate have 4 kcal per gram, fat has 9. So grams = calories for that macro ÷ 4 or ÷ 9. 750 kcal of protein is 187.5 g.
calculate-macros.s2b: 2500 kcal, maintain weight and a balanced split are set. The grams sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-macros.s3b: Type your maintenance calories. Lose weight subtracts 500 kcal; gain adds 300. 2500 maintenance becomes 2000 to lose weight.
calculate-macros.s4b: Balanced is 30/30/40 (protein/fat/carbs %), high protein 40/30/30, low carb 35/45/20. 2000 kcal high protein is 200 g protein, 67 g fat and 150 g carbs.
calculate-macros.s5b: Type your weight. 200 g at 70 kg is 2.9 g per kg; active adults often aim for 1.6–2.2. Pick a lower-protein split if yours is far above that.
calculate-macros.s6t: Turn grams into meals, then copy
calculate-macros.s6b: Divide by the number of meals: 200 g protein over four meals is 50 g each. Copy puts the target and grams on the clipboard.
calculate-macros.diagram1: Grams = calories × share ÷ 4 for protein and carbs, ÷ 9 for fat.
calculate-macros.diagram2: 2500 kcal at 30/30/40: 188 g protein, 83 g fat, 250 g carbs.

calories-burned-exercise.name: How to calculate calories burned during exercise
calories-burned-exercise.blurb: Calories = MET × body weight in kg × hours. 30 minutes at 70 kg: running at 10 km/h about 343 kcal, jumping rope 413, cycling 280, swimming 203, yoga 88.
calories-burned-exercise.title: How to calculate calories burned during exercise
calories-burned-exercise.lead: You want to know what a workout burns. You will pick an activity, enter your weight and minutes, and read the calories from its MET value. 30 minutes of running at 10 km/h at 70 kg burns about 343 kcal. Nothing leaves this tab.
calories-burned-exercise.result: Calories burned, calories per minute, the MET value, a fat equivalent and the same minutes for 15 other activities.
calories-burned-exercise.note: Open the calories burned calculator after the workout or while planning it. MET values are averages; your real burn can differ by 20% or more. Nothing is uploaded.
calories-burned-exercise.s1b: One MET is the energy you use sitting still, about 1 kcal per kg per hour. Running at 10 km/h is 9.8 MET, nearly ten times rest. Calories = MET × kg × hours.
calories-burned-exercise.s2t: Open Calories burned calculator on cv.cm
calories-burned-exercise.s2b: Brisk walking, 70 kg and 30 minutes are set. The result and a comparison list sit on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
calories-burned-exercise.s3b: Type your weight in kg or switch to lb, and the minutes. Heavier people burn more for the same activity, because the formula scales with weight.
calories-burned-exercise.s4b: Choose from 16 activities with MET values from the 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities. Running at 10 km/h for 30 minutes at 70 kg: 9.8 × 70 × 0.5 = 343 kcal.
calories-burned-exercise.s5b: The list below shows the same 30 minutes for every activity, highest first: jumping rope 413, running 343, cycling 280, swimming 203, yoga 88.
calories-burned-exercise.s6t: Subtract rest if you want the extra only, then copy
calories-burned-exercise.s6b: MET counts the energy you would burn anyway. For the extra from exercise only, subtract about 1 kcal per kg per hour: 35 kcal for 30 minutes at 70 kg. Copy puts the result on the clipboard.
calories-burned-exercise.diagram1: Calories = MET × kg × hours; one MET ≈ 1 kcal per kg per hour at rest.
calories-burned-exercise.diagram2: 30 minutes at 70 kg: jumping rope 413, running 343, cycling 280, swimming 203, yoga 88 kcal.

compound-interest.name: How to calculate compound interest
compound-interest.blurb: Future value = principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years). 1000 at 5% for 10 years grows to 1628.89 compounded yearly, 1647.01 monthly and 1648.66 daily.
compound-interest.title: How to calculate compound interest
compound-interest.lead: You have a deposit or an investment and a yearly rate. You will see what it grows to when interest earns interest, and how often compounding changes the result. 1000 at 5% for 10 years compounded monthly becomes 1647.01, of which 647.01 is interest. Nothing leaves this tab.
compound-interest.result: The future value and the total interest for your principal, rate, years and compounding frequency.
compound-interest.note: Open the compound interest calculator with the principal, the yearly rate and the term at hand. It assumes no deposits or withdrawals along the way and no tax. Nothing is uploaded.
compound-interest.s1b: Future value = principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years), where n is how many times a year interest is added. Each period's interest is added to the balance, so the next period earns interest on it too.
compound-interest.s2b: 1000, 5% a year, 10 years and monthly compounding are filled. The future value sits on the right. Nothing is uploaded.
compound-interest.s3b: Type the starting amount, the yearly rate in percent and the number of years. Use the nominal rate (APR) the bank quotes, not the effective rate.
compound-interest.s4b: Yearly gives 1628.89, quarterly 1643.62, monthly 1647.01, daily 1648.66. More frequent compounding adds a little each step, with diminishing gains.
compound-interest.s5b: Simple interest would pay 5% of 1000 each year, 500 over 10 years. Compounding adds 147.01 more. The gap widens with higher rates and longer terms.
compound-interest.s6b: The rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ rate. At 5% that is about 14.4 years. Copy puts the future value and interest on the clipboard.
compound-interest.diagram1: Future value = principal × (1 + rate ÷ n)^(n × years).
compound-interest.diagram2: 1000 at 5% for 10 years: yearly 1628.89, monthly 1647.01, daily 1648.66.

remove-photo-background.name: How to remove the background from a photo for free
remove-photo-background.blurb: Drop JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC photos and an AI model cuts out the subject in your browser. Pick transparent, white, a color or blur, then download PNG, WebP or JPG, or all at once as a ZIP.
remove-photo-background.title: How to remove the background from a photo for free
remove-photo-background.lead: You have a photo of a person, a product or a pet and want it on a clean background. You will drop the photo, let an AI model cut out the subject in this tab and download the result. Photos never leave your device.
remove-photo-background.result: A cut-out with a transparent, white, colored or blurred background, downloaded as PNG, WebP or JPG, or several as one ZIP.
remove-photo-background.note: Open the background remover on a computer or a recent phone. The first run downloads the model once; later runs start at once. Your photos are never uploaded.
remove-photo-background.s1b: The subject should be in focus and stand out from the background. Hair against a busy background is the hardest case; a plain wall or sky gives the cleanest edge.
remove-photo-background.s2b: The drop zone accepts JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC. The model runs in this tab on your graphics card when possible, otherwise on the processor.

remove-photo-background.s5b: Transparent keeps only the subject. White suits product listings and ID-style photos. Color fills any color; Blur keeps the scene softly out of focus behind the subject.

test-regex.name: How to test a regular expression
test-regex.blurb: Type a pattern, set the g, i, m, s and u flags and paste text to see every match with its capture groups. A replacement such as [$&] or $1 previews the result before you use it in code.
test-regex.title: How to test a regular expression
test-regex.lead: You are writing a pattern for code, a search box or a spreadsheet and want to see what it matches before you use it. You will type the pattern, paste sample text and read every match. \b\w+@\w+\.\w+\b finds simple email addresses. Nothing leaves this tab.
test-regex.result: The number of matches, each match with its position and capture groups, and an optional replace preview, using JavaScript regular expressions.
test-regex.note: Open the regex tester with a few lines of real text, including lines that should not match. It uses the JavaScript flavour, the same as browsers and Node.js. Nothing is uploaded.
test-regex.s1b: \d is a digit, \w a letter, digit or underscore, \s a space, . any character. + means one or more, * zero or more, ? optional. ( ) captures a group; \b is a word boundary.
test-regex.s2b: The pattern box, the flags and the test text are ready. Nothing is uploaded.
test-regex.s3t: Type the pattern and paste text
test-regex.s3b: Type the pattern without slashes, for example \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} for dates such as 2026-10-29. Paste text with lines that should and should not match.
test-regex.s4b: g finds every match instead of the first; i ignores case; m makes ^ and $ work per line; s lets . match line breaks; u enables full Unicode. The match count line shows the active flags.
test-regex.s5b: Each match lists its text and capture groups. (\d{4})-(\d{2}) on 2026-10 gives group 1 = 2026 and group 2 = 10. A pattern that matches too much usually needs \b or a narrower class.
test-regex.s6b: Type a replacement: $& is the whole match, $1 the first group. [$&] wraps each match in brackets. Copy matches puts every match on the clipboard.
test-regex.diagram1: \d digit, \w word character, \s space, + one or more, ( ) capture group, \b word boundary.
test-regex.diagram2: Flags: g all matches, i ignore case, m per line, s dot matches newline, u Unicode.

watermark.q1: Does adding a watermark upload my photos?
watermark.a1: No. ID copies and photos stay in this tab. The canvas stamps the mark here. Closing the tab discards the files. Export also strips EXIF.
watermark.q2: What is the invisible watermark, and can it trace a leak?
watermark.a2: On export the tool hides the same text as the visible mark (or your own, such as “Bank A”), plus “cv.cm” and the export date, in the image brightness. It is on by default and can be switched off under Invisible watermark. If a copy turns up elsewhere, drop it on “Check an image for a hidden mark” to read it, even after the visible mark was painted over. It survives JPEG compression and resizing; cropping or rotation can break it. Short text holds up best. It is a lead, not legal proof.
watermark.q3: Can I watermark an ID or passport copy?
watermark.a3: Yes. Use For-use only so a tiled “for [org] use only” line covers the photo. Open Redact to black out the ID number too. Work stays in this tab. A watermark is a deterrent, not a legal guarantee. Some offices still want an unmarked copy.
watermark.a4: No. This tool only adds a mark. It will not erase watermarks from photos.
watermark.a5: PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF in. Export PNG, JPEG, or WebP. Text, a logo, or both. Add a batch and download one file or a ZIP.

profit-margin.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

convert-base.q1: Can I convert between bases free online?
convert-base.a1: Yes. cv.cm converts one integer between bases 2 and 36 in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
convert-base.a2: FF. From base 10 to base 16. The letters are uppercase.
convert-base.q3: Can I type 0x or a decimal point?
convert-base.a3: No. Type the digits only. A fraction is not an integer in a base.
convert-base.q4: Is this the tool that turns text into binary?
convert-base.a4: No. This converts one integer. The binary tool turns letters into 8-bit groups.
convert-base.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

add-duration.q1: Can I add hours and minutes free online?
add-duration.a1: Yes. cv.cm adds or subtracts two H:MM:SS lengths in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
add-duration.q2: What format do the times use?
add-duration.a2: Hours:minutes:seconds, such as 1:30:00. Minutes and seconds must be 0–59. 0:90:00 fails. Write 1:30:00.
add-duration.q4: What if the second time is longer?
add-duration.a4: Subtracting it gives a negative length, such as -0:15:00. That is a direction, not a clock time.
add-duration.q5: Is this a time zone converter?
add-duration.a5: No. These are lengths of time. A clock time in a city is the time-zone tool.

calculate-percent.q1: Can I calculate a percentage free online?
calculate-percent.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows four readings of the same two numbers in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-percent.a2: 50. That is the first line when the boxes are 25 and 200.
calculate-percent.a3: 12.5%. That is the second line, not the first.
calculate-percent.a4: 250. That is the third line. The change from 200 down to 25 is -87.5%, which is the fourth line.
calculate-percent.q5: What if the second number is zero?
calculate-percent.a5: What-percent and percent-change become a dash. You cannot divide by zero. The other two lines still run.

days-between.q1: Can I count days between two dates free online?
days-between.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows the signed days, the absolute days, and whole weeks in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
days-between.q2: Does the count include both dates?
days-between.a2: No. The same day is 0. Monday 5 January 2026 to Friday 9 January is 4. A form that includes both dates wants 5.
days-between.a3: No. Weekends stay in this count. The business-day page skips Saturday and Sunday and includes both ends.
days-between.a4: Yes, when the leap day sits in the gap. 28 February 2024 to 1 March 2024 is 2 days.
days-between.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

shift-date.q1: Can I add days to a date free online?
shift-date.a1: Yes. cv.cm shifts a civil date by a whole number of days in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
shift-date.q2: Can the number be negative or a fraction?
shift-date.a2: Negative numbers go backward. 1.5 is rejected. Only a whole number of days works.
shift-date.a3: 29 February 2024. In 2023 the same step lands on 1 March.
shift-date.q4: Does Friday plus 1 skip the weekend?
shift-date.a4: No. Friday plus 1 is Saturday. Add 3 to land on Monday.
shift-date.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

iso-week.q1: Can I find an ISO week number free online?
iso-week.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows the ISO year, week, and weekday in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
iso-week.a2: Monday. Monday is 1 and Sunday is 7. A Sunday-start week is a different number.
iso-week.q3: Can January belong to the previous year?
iso-week.a3: Yes. 1 January 2021 is a Friday in 2020-W53. Week 1 is the week with the first Thursday.
iso-week.q4: Can late December belong to the next year?
iso-week.a4: Yes. 30 December 2024 is a Monday in 2025-W01.
iso-week.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

vat-price.q1: Can I add VAT to a price free online?
vat-price.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows net, tax, and gross in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
vat-price.a3: Net 100.00, tax 20.00, gross 120.00. The tax is not 24.00.
vat-price.q4: Does the page look up a country rate?
vat-price.a4: No. You type the rate. The three lines are arithmetic, not a tax filing, and they do not name a currency.
vat-price.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

percent-off.q1: Can I calculate a discount free online?
percent-off.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows the sale price and the saving in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
percent-off.a2: Sale price 80.00, saving 20.00. That is not a 20% profit margin.
percent-off.a3: Yes. 120% off 100 is a sale price of -20.00. That is arithmetic, not a shop rule.
percent-off.q4: What does a negative percent do?
percent-off.a4: It raises the price. Minus 10% on 100 is 110.00. A tag that says 10% off uses 10.
percent-off.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it. The numbers have no currency.

encode-url.q1: Can I encode a URL free online?
encode-url.a1: Yes. cv.cm encodes and decodes the string in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
encode-url.a2: Encode writes %20. Decode turns %20 and + into a space.
encode-url.q3: Will slashes stay if I encode a whole address?
encode-url.a3: No. : and / become %3A and %2F. Encode a query value when the address itself must stay openable.
encode-url.a4: A % needs two hex digits after it. %zz and a lone % fail.
encode-url.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

calculate-age.q1: Can I calculate age free online?
calculate-age.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows years, months, days, and total days in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-age.q2: Does the year increase before the birthday?
calculate-age.a2: No. Born 15 March 2000, on 14 March 2026 the age is still 25 years, 11 months, and 27 days.
calculate-age.q3: What if the later date is before the birth date?
calculate-age.a3: The page fails. Age counts forward from the birth date.
calculate-age.q4: Is 29 February a real birth date?
calculate-age.a4: Yes. On 28 February 2025, a 29 February 2000 birth is 24 years, 11 months, and 30 days.
calculate-age.a5: No. Closing the tab discards them.

aspect-ratio.q1: Can I find an aspect ratio free online?
aspect-ratio.a1: Yes. cv.cm reduces width and height in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
aspect-ratio.a3: No. It only reduces the two numbers. The picture stays the size you typed.
aspect-ratio.a4: Each side is rounded to a whole pixel before the ratio.
aspect-ratio.a5: No. Closing the tab discards them.

calculate-bmi.q1: Can I calculate BMI free online?
calculate-bmi.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows the BMI and the band in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-bmi.q2: What is the BMI for 70 kg and 170 cm?
calculate-bmi.q3: What if I type 1.70 for the height?
calculate-bmi.a3: The box is centimetres, so 1.70 means 1.70 cm. The BMI becomes 242214.5. Type 170.
calculate-bmi.a4: At 25. 18.5 is still Normal. Obesity starts at 30.
calculate-bmi.a5: No. Closing the tab discards them. The band is not a diagnosis.

split-tip.q1: Can I split a tip free online?
split-tip.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows the tip, the total, and each share in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
split-tip.q2: What does each person pay on 100 at 20% for 4 people?
split-tip.a2: 30.00. The tip is 20.00 and the total is 120.00. 5.00 would be the tip split alone.
split-tip.a3: It counts as 2. The fraction is dropped. On 100 at 20%, each of those 2 pays 60.00.
split-tip.q4: What if the people count is below 1?
split-tip.a4: The page fails. 0.9 is not rounded up to 1.
