split-tip.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it. The numbers have no currency.

loan-payment.q1: Can I calculate a loan payment free online?
loan-payment.a1: Yes. cv.cm shows the monthly payment, the interest, and the total in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
loan-payment.q2: What is the payment on 10000 at 12% for one year?
loan-payment.a2: 888.49 a month. Interest is 661.85 and the total is 10661.85. It is not 1200 of interest.
loan-payment.q3: What does a zero interest rate do?
loan-payment.a3: It divides the principal by the number of months. 12000 for one year is 1000.00 a month and 0.00 interest.
loan-payment.q4: Does 12 in the rate box mean 0.12?
loan-payment.a4: No. 12 means 12% a year. The monthly rate is that percent divided by 12. One year is 12 payments, not one.
loan-payment.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it. The page does not name a lender or a currency.

read-cron.q1: Can I read a cron expression free online?
read-cron.a1: Yes. cv.cm describes the five fields in this tab. Nothing is uploaded, and the job is not started.
read-cron.a2: Minute 0, hour 9, every day of the month, every month, and Monday.
read-cron.a3: 0 and 7. Monday is 1. The word MON fails.
read-cron.q4: Why did a six-field expression fail?
read-cron.a4: This page wants exactly five fields. There is no seconds field. Minute 60 also fails, because minutes stop at 59.
read-cron.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it. The page does not run the schedule.

mosaic-photo.q1: How do I pixelate part of a photo without an app?
mosaic-photo.a1: Open cv.cm mosaic, drop the photo, drag a box, and download. It runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
mosaic-photo.q2: Is a mosaic enough to hide an ID number?
mosaic-photo.a2: Not always. Fine cells can leave digits readable. Use a black box for numbers and QR codes.
mosaic-photo.q3: Can someone remove the mosaic later?
mosaic-photo.a3: Not from your export. The covered pixels are replaced, not layered on top.
mosaic-photo.q4: Can I hide faces in a group photo?
mosaic-photo.a4: Yes. Draw one box per face. Each photo keeps its own boxes.
mosaic-photo.a5: No. Closing the tab discards it.

watermark-id-copy.q1: What should I write on an ID copy watermark?
watermark-id-copy.a1: Who it is for, what for, and the date, such as “For XX bank account opening only. Not valid otherwise. 2026-10-08”.
watermark-id-copy.q2: Should the watermark cover the photo?
watermark-id-copy.a2: Yes. Tile it so it crosses the portrait; a corner mark is easy to crop off.
watermark-id-copy.q3: Is a watermarked ID copy still valid?
watermark-id-copy.a3: A watermark deters misuse but is not a legal guarantee. Some counters require an unmarked copy; ask first.
watermark-id-copy.a4: No. It stays in this tab, and closing it discards the file. Export also removes EXIF.
watermark-id-copy.q5: Can I hide the ID number too?
watermark-id-copy.a5: Yes. Use Redact with a black box on the fields the receiver did not ask for.

find-bedtime.q1: Can I find a bedtime free online?
find-bedtime.a1: Yes. cv.cm counts the cycles in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
find-bedtime.a2: Five cycles of 90 minutes is 450 minutes, plus 14 minutes to fall asleep, counted back from 07:00.
find-bedtime.q3: How many hours should I sleep?
find-bedtime.a3: Five or six cycles, 7.5 to 9 hours, suit most adults. Three or four cycles are shown for nights when you have no choice.
find-bedtime.a4: No. Cycles range from about 70 to 120 minutes and change through the night. Treat the times as a starting point and adjust by how you feel.
find-bedtime.a5: No. It only lists times. Set the alarm on your phone or clock.

measure-body-fat.q1: Can I estimate body fat free online?
measure-body-fat.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs the U.S. Navy formula in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
measure-body-fat.a2: Height, neck and waist for men; height, neck, waist and hips for women. Weight is optional and only splits fat and lean mass.
measure-body-fat.a3: At the navel for men and at the narrowest point for women, tape level and snug.
measure-body-fat.q4: How accurate is the tape method?
measure-body-fat.a4: Within about 3 to 4 percentage points of a DEXA scan for most adults. It is better for tracking change than for one exact number.
measure-body-fat.q5: What is a healthy body fat?
measure-body-fat.a5: By the ACE ranges, fitness is 14–17% for men and 21–24% for women, and average is 18–24% and 25–31%. Ask a doctor about your own case.

check-contrast.q1: Can I check color contrast free online?
check-contrast.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes the WCAG ratio in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
check-contrast.q2: What ratio does normal text need?
check-contrast.a2: 4.5:1 for AA and 7:1 for AAA. Large text needs 3:1 and 4.5:1.
check-contrast.q4: Does the order of the colors matter?
check-contrast.a4: No. The ratio is the same either way. Swap only changes the preview.
check-contrast.a5: Its ratio on white is 4.48:1, just under 4.5:1. #767676 reaches 4.54:1 and passes.

calculate-pace.q1: Can I calculate running pace free online?
calculate-pace.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-pace.q2: What is 10 km in 55 minutes as pace?
calculate-pace.a2: 5:30 per km, 8:51 per mile, or 10.91 km/h.
calculate-pace.q3: How do I convert pace per km to per mile?
calculate-pace.a3: Multiply by 1.609. The page shows both at once.
calculate-pace.a4: They assume you hold the same pace. Most runners slow a little over longer distances, so treat them as a best case.
calculate-pace.a5: h:mm:ss or mm:ss, such as 1:45:29 or 55:00. Pace takes m:ss, such as 5:30.

calculate-final-grade.q1: Can I find the grade I need on a final free online?
calculate-final-grade.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-final-grade.a2: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight, with the weight as a fraction such as 0.30.
calculate-final-grade.q3: What if I need more than 100%?
calculate-final-grade.a3: The target is out of reach on the final alone. Check the table for the highest letter you can still get.
calculate-final-grade.a4: Your weighted average on everything graded before the final, as your gradebook shows it.
calculate-final-grade.q5: Does the weight of the final matter a lot?
calculate-final-grade.a5: Yes. With 85% now and 90% wanted, a 30% final needs 101.7% but a 50% final needs only 95%.

calculate-tdee.q1: Can I calculate TDEE free online?
calculate-tdee.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
calculate-tdee.a2: Mifflin–St Jeor for BMR: 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age, plus 5 for men or minus 161 for women. TDEE is BMR × activity factor.
calculate-tdee.q3: How much should I cut to lose weight?
calculate-tdee.a3: The page subtracts 500 kcal, about 0.5 kg a week, but never below 1500 kcal for men or 1200 for women.
calculate-tdee.a4: Most desk workers who exercise 1–3 times a week are light; 3–5 times is moderate. When unsure, pick the lower one.
calculate-tdee.a5: No. It is an estimate for healthy adults. Ask a doctor or dietitian before a big change.

calculate-gpa.q1: Can I calculate GPA free online?
calculate-gpa.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-gpa.a2: Each grade becomes points, multiplied by the course credits. The sum of points is divided by the sum of credits.
calculate-gpa.a3: By default A+ is 4.0. Tick A+ = 4.3 if your school uses that scale.
calculate-gpa.a4: Usually not. Leave them out of the list.
calculate-gpa.q5: How do I get a cumulative GPA?
calculate-gpa.a5: Put every course from every term in one list. The result is weighted by credits across all of them.

use-pomodoro.q1: Can I use a Pomodoro timer free online?
use-pomodoro.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs it in this tab. Nothing is sent or stored.
use-pomodoro.a2: Work for 25 minutes, rest 5, and take a 15-minute break after four blocks. Each block is one pomodoro.
use-pomodoro.q3: Will it chime in a background tab?
use-pomodoro.a3: Yes, while the tab stays open. The timer follows the clock and the tab title shows the time left.
use-pomodoro.a4: Yes, from 1 to 180 minutes for each phase and 1 to 12 rounds, while the clock is stopped.
use-pomodoro.a5: No. Only finished focus blocks count toward the long break.

find-due-date.q1: Can I calculate a due date free online?
find-due-date.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
find-due-date.a2: Due date = first day of the last period + 280 days + (cycle length − 28).
find-due-date.q3: What if I only know the conception date?
find-due-date.a3: Pick Conception date; the due date is 266 days after it.
find-due-date.a4: Naegele's rule assumes ovulation on day 14 of a 28-day cycle. Enter your own cycle length and the tool shifts the dates.
find-due-date.a5: No. It is an estimate. An early ultrasound gives the most reliable date.

find-ideal-weight.q1: Can I find my ideal weight free online?
find-ideal-weight.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
find-ideal-weight.a2: None alone. Read the spread of the four as a range and check it against the BMI row.
find-ideal-weight.q3: What is the ideal weight for 170 cm?
find-ideal-weight.a3: About 65.2 to 66.7 kg for a man and 60.7 to 62.5 kg for a woman by the four formulas; the BMI 18.5–24.9 range is 53.5 to 72 kg.
find-ideal-weight.a4: Yes, down to 140 cm: the formulas extrapolate their per-inch step below 152.4 cm, so treat those results as rough.
find-ideal-weight.a5: No. The formulas come from dosing tables. A doctor or dietitian can set a personal target.

daily-water.q1: Can I calculate my water intake free online?
daily-water.a1: Yes. cv.cm computes it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
daily-water.q2: How much water should a 70 kg person drink?
daily-water.a2: About 2.45 litres at rest, 2.8 litres with 30 minutes of exercise, and 3.3 litres in hot weather.
daily-water.a3: Yes. They are mostly water. Food also supplies roughly a fifth of daily fluid.
daily-water.q4: Is eight glasses a day right?
daily-water.a4: Eight 250 ml glasses is 2 litres, which fits a 57 kg person at rest. Heavier, active people need more; the calculator scales it.
daily-water.a5: No. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or heart conditions and some medicines change the need. Ask a doctor.

trip-fuel-cost.q1: Can I calculate fuel cost free online?
trip-fuel-cost.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
trip-fuel-cost.q2: How do I convert mpg to L/100 km?
trip-fuel-cost.a2: Divide 235.2 by the mpg: 30 mpg is 7.84 L/100 km. The tool does it when you pick mpg.
trip-fuel-cost.q3: What does 300 km cost at 7 L/100 km?
trip-fuel-cost.a3: 21 litres. At 1.60 a litre that is 33.60; the round trip is 67.20.
trip-fuel-cost.a4: None. The result is in whatever you type for the price.
trip-fuel-cost.q5: Why is my real cost higher?
trip-fuel-cost.a5: City traffic, air conditioning, roof racks and a loaded car raise consumption. Add about 10%.

estimate-reading-time.q1: Can I estimate reading time free online?
estimate-reading-time.a1: Yes. cv.cm counts it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
estimate-reading-time.q2: How many words is a five-minute read?
estimate-reading-time.a2: About 1200 at the average 238 words a minute. Many sites use 200–250 wpm, so 1000–1250.
estimate-reading-time.q3: How many words is a five-minute speech?
estimate-reading-time.a3: About 650 at 130 words a minute. Slow, clear speakers use 550–600.
estimate-reading-time.a4: In characters: 300 a minute for reading and 180 for speaking. Mixed text counts Latin words and CJK characters together.
estimate-reading-time.a5: Yes, with and without spaces, for post and ad limits.

compare-text.q1: Can I compare two texts free online?
compare-text.a1: Yes. cv.cm diffs them in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
compare-text.a2: The left. Lines only on the right are added (+), lines only on the left are removed (−).
compare-text.a3: Yes. Tick Ignore extra spaces to skip whitespace-only changes.
compare-text.a4: The standard patch format with --- and +++ headers and @@ hunks, used by git and code reviews. Copy unified diff produces it.
compare-text.q5: Does it compare words inside a line?
compare-text.a5: No. It works line by line; a changed line shows as one removed and one added.

hash-text.q1: Can I hash a file free online without uploading it?
hash-text.a1: Yes. cv.cm reads the file in this tab with Web Crypto. Nothing is uploaded.
hash-text.a2: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512, in hex and Base64.
hash-text.q3: Why does my hash not match?
hash-text.a3: A different algorithm, an extra space or line break, or a different file. Check the algorithm first.
hash-text.a4: For checking a download against a listed checksum, yes. For passwords or signatures, no; use SHA-256 or better.
hash-text.q5: Can I verify a password hash here?
hash-text.a5: Only plain digests. Salted hashes such as bcrypt need their own tools.

generate-uuid.q1: Can I generate a UUID free online?
generate-uuid.a1: Yes. cv.cm makes them in this tab with Web Crypto. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
generate-uuid.a2: Version 4, random. The third group starts with 4.
generate-uuid.a3: In practice, no: 122 random bits give about 5.3 × 10^36 values.
generate-uuid.q4: Can I get them without hyphens?
generate-uuid.a4: Yes. Untick Hyphens for the 32-character form.
generate-uuid.a5: No. They exist only in this tab until you copy them.

calculate-work-hours.q1: Can I calculate hours worked free online?
calculate-work-hours.a1: Yes. cv.cm adds the shifts in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-work-hours.q2: How many hours is 9 to 5:30 with a 30-minute break?
calculate-work-hours.a2: 8 hours. 8.5 hours on the clock minus the unpaid break.
calculate-work-hours.q3: How do I convert 7 hours 45 minutes to decimal?
calculate-work-hours.a3: Divide the minutes by 60: 45 ÷ 60 = 0.75, so 7.75 hours.
calculate-work-hours.a4: Yes. An end time before the start runs past midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours.
calculate-work-hours.q5: Is the overtime rule right for my job?
calculate-work-hours.a5: The default is over 40 hours a week at 1.5×. Some places count daily overtime or use 2×; set the threshold and multiplier to your rules.

electricity-cost.q1: Can I calculate appliance electricity cost free online?
electricity-cost.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
electricity-cost.q2: How much does a 1000 W appliance cost per hour?
electricity-cost.a2: It uses 1 kWh an hour, so the cost equals your price per kWh, for example 0.15.
electricity-cost.q3: How do I convert amps to watts?
electricity-cost.a3: Multiply amps by volts: 5 A at 220 V is 1100 W, at 120 V it is 600 W.
electricity-cost.q4: Why is my fridge's real use lower?
electricity-cost.a4: The compressor runs only part of the time, often about a third, so the label watts overstate daily use.
electricity-cost.a5: Whatever you type for the price. The result is in the same currency.

find-fertile-window.q1: Can I calculate my ovulation day free online?
find-fertile-window.a1: Yes. cv.cm estimates it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or stored.
find-fertile-window.q2: When do I ovulate with a 28-day cycle?
find-fertile-window.a2: Around day 14, counting the first day of your period as day 1.
find-fertile-window.q3: How long is the fertile window?
find-fertile-window.a3: About six days: the five days before ovulation plus ovulation day.
find-fertile-window.q4: Can I use this to avoid pregnancy?
find-fertile-window.a4: No. Calendar estimates are not reliable contraception. Use a proper method and ask a doctor.
find-fertile-window.q5: My cycle is irregular. What should I enter?
find-fertile-window.a5: The average of your last six cycles. Irregular cycles make the estimate less accurate; ovulation tests help.

calculate-macros.q1: Can I calculate macros free online?
calculate-macros.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calculate-macros.q2: How many grams of protein is 30% of 2000 kcal?
calculate-macros.a3: A gram of fat has 9 kcal; protein and carbohydrate have 4.
calculate-macros.a4: Balanced suits most people. High protein helps keep muscle while losing weight; low carb suits people who prefer fewer carbs.
calculate-macros.q5: Where do I get my calories?
calculate-macros.a5: From the TDEE calculator, which estimates maintenance calories from age, size and activity.

calories-burned-exercise.q1: Can I calculate calories burned free online?
calories-burned-exercise.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
calories-burned-exercise.q2: How many calories does 30 minutes of running burn?
calories-burned-exercise.a2: About 343 kcal at 10 km/h for a 70 kg person; about 290 at 60 kg.
calories-burned-exercise.a3: The energy of an activity compared with sitting still. 1 MET is about 1 kcal per kg per hour.
calories-burned-exercise.a4: Within about 20% for most people. Fitness, effort and terrain change the real number.
calories-burned-exercise.q5: Where do the values come from?
calories-burned-exercise.a5: The 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities by Ainsworth and colleagues.

compound-interest.q1: Can I calculate compound interest free online?
compound-interest.a1: Yes. cv.cm does the math in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
compound-interest.q3: What is the difference from simple interest?
compound-interest.a3: Simple interest pays only on the original amount; compound interest also pays on interest already added.
compound-interest.q4: How long does it take to double?
compound-interest.a4: About 72 ÷ the rate in years: 14.4 years at 5%, 9 years at 8%.
compound-interest.a5: No. It shows one starting amount growing with no deposits, withdrawals or tax.

remove-photo-background.q1: Can I remove a photo background for free?
remove-photo-background.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs the AI model in your browser at no cost, with no sign-up and no watermark.
remove-photo-background.a2: No. The model downloads to your browser and the photos stay on your device.
remove-photo-background.q3: Why is the first run slow?
remove-photo-background.a3: The model downloads once. Later runs use the cached copy.
remove-photo-background.a4: PNG and WebP. JPG has no transparency, so it gets a white background.
remove-photo-background.q5: Can I do several photos at once?
remove-photo-background.a5: Yes. Drop several and use Download all (ZIP).

test-regex.q1: Can I test a regex free online?
test-regex.a1: Yes. cv.cm runs it in this tab. Nothing is uploaded.
test-regex.a2: JavaScript, the same as browsers and Node.js. Most simple patterns work the same in Python and Java.
test-regex.q3: Why do I only get one match?
test-regex.a3: Turn on the g flag to find every match.
test-regex.q4: How do I use a capture group in the replacement?
test-regex.a4: $1 is the first group, $2 the second, $& the whole match.
test-regex.a5: No. Type only the pattern; flags are checkboxes.

compress-pdf.q1: Can I compress a PDF here?
compress-pdf.a1: Yes. This PDF compressor redraws each page as JPEG and packs a new PDF in this tab.
compress-pdf.a2: No. pdf.js renders locally. Closing the tab discards it.
compress-pdf.q3: Will the file always get smaller?
compress-pdf.a3: Usually for scans and photo PDFs. An already-tiny text PDF may not shrink much.
compress-pdf.a4: No. Pages become images, so text is no longer selectable.
compress-pdf.q5: What do quality and resolution do?
compress-pdf.a5: Quality is JPEG compression. 1× is smaller; 2× is sharper and heavier.

split-pdf.q1: Can I split a PDF into pages?
split-pdf.a1: Yes. Each page becomes its own PDF, packed in a ZIP when there are several.
split-pdf.q2: Can I keep only some pages?
split-pdf.a2: Yes. Use a range like 1-3,5 and download one PDF with those pages.
split-pdf.a3: No. pdf-lib runs in this tab.
split-pdf.a4: Often not. Unlock the file first.
split-pdf.a5: Pages are copied. Bookmarks and forms may be dropped.

names.a1: Yes. It makes random given+family names or usernames in this tab.
names.a2: No. They are random combinations for mockups, games, or handles — not legal identities.
names.a3: Yes. Switch to username for adjective+noun handles, sometimes with digits.
names.a4: No. Generation uses Web Crypto locally.
names.q5: Can I copy the whole list?
names.a5: Yes. Copy list puts every line on the clipboard.

timezone.q1: How do I convert a time zone?
timezone.a1: Pick the source zone, the destination zone, and a date-time. The result is the same instant shown on the other clock.
timezone.a2: Yes. Conversion uses IANA zones, so New York switches between EST and EDT automatically.
timezone.a3: No. Intl.DateTimeFormat runs in this tab. Closing it discards the conversion.
timezone.a4: It is the same instant as ISO-8601 in UTC, useful for APIs, logs, and calendars.
timezone.a5: Common cities first, then every IANA zone the browser knows, including UTC.

lorem.q1: What is a lorem ipsum generator?
lorem.a1: It fills a layout with classic Latin-like placeholder text so you can judge spacing before the real copy is ready.
lorem.q2: Can I choose paragraphs or words?
lorem.a2: Yes. Switch among paragraphs, sentences, and words, then drag the count slider.
lorem.a3: It follows the usual dummy-text word list. It is not a translation of a real passage.
lorem.a4: No. The text is built from a local word list in this tab.
lorem.a5: Yes. Copy puts the whole block on the clipboard so you can paste it into a mockup.

units.a1: Choose a category, a from-unit and a to-unit, then type a number. The result updates in this tab.
units.q2: Can I convert cm to inches?
units.a2: Yes. Length includes mm, cm, m, km, inches, feet, yards, and miles.
units.a3: Temperature converts among °C, °F, and kelvin, including the offset, not just a scale factor.
units.q4: Are these US or imperial gallons?
units.a4: Volume uses US customary cups, fluid ounces, and gallons. Length and mass use the international yard and pound.
units.a5: No. The arithmetic runs in this tab. Closing it discards the numbers.

barcode.q1: Can I generate a barcode here?
barcode.a1: Yes. Code 128, Code 39, and EAN-13 draw in this tab. Download a PNG when it looks right.
barcode.a2: Code 128 holds letters and digits for labels and shipping. EAN-13 is the 13-digit retail product barcode.
barcode.a3: No. Encoding and drawing stay in this tab. Closing it discards the image.
barcode.a4: Phone cameras and USB scanners read these formats when printed with enough size and contrast.
barcode.q5: When should I use a QR code instead?
barcode.a5: Use the QR tool for URLs and longer text. Barcodes are for short IDs and product numbers.

meme.q1: Can I make a meme here?
meme.a1: Yes. Drop a photo, type top and bottom captions, then download a PNG. Nothing is uploaded.
meme.a2: Classic meme style: Impact or a heavy sans, white fill and a black outline.
meme.a3: No. Drawing stays in this tab. Closing it discards the image.
meme.a4: Yes. Paste or drop PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or HEIC when the browser can decode it.
meme.q5: How is this different from watermark?
meme.a5: Watermark is for a logo or copyright mark. This tool is for large top and bottom captions.

text-to-speech.q1: Can I convert text to speech here?
text-to-speech.a1: Yes. Paste text, pick a voice, and press Speak. The browser reads it with voices already on your device.
text-to-speech.a2: No. SpeechSynthesis runs in this tab. Closing it stops playback.
text-to-speech.a3: No. The browser voice engine does not give an audio file, so this tool only plays sound.
text-to-speech.q4: Why is the voice list empty?
text-to-speech.a4: Some browsers fill voices after a moment, or they have none installed. Chrome, Safari, and Edge usually work.
text-to-speech.q5: Does it support Chinese or other languages?
text-to-speech.a5: If your system has that language pack, it appears in the list. The page does not fetch cloud voices.

invoice.q1: Can I generate an invoice PDF here?
invoice.a1: Yes. Fill from/to, line items, tax, and currency, then download a one-page A4 PDF.
invoice.q2: Is this an official tax invoice?
invoice.a2: No. It is a simple PDF you fill in. Not accounting software and not a government tax form.
invoice.a3: No. The page is drawn in this tab and packed into a PDF here. Closing the tab discards it.
invoice.a4: Yes. The PDF is a page image, so it can include any language your browser can draw.
invoice.a5: USD, EUR, GBP, CNY, JPY, KRW, VND, and IDR. Amounts use the browser's currency format.

signature.q1: Can I generate a signature here?
signature.a1: Yes. Draw with a mouse or finger, then download a cropped PNG. Nothing is uploaded.
signature.q2: Is this a legally binding e-signature?
signature.a2: No. It is a picture of a drawing. It is not DocuSign and not a qualified electronic signature.
signature.a3: No. The pad runs in this tab. Closing it discards the strokes.
signature.q4: Does the PNG have a transparent background?
signature.a4: Yes. Export crops to the ink and keeps a transparent background for placing on documents.
signature.a5: Yes. Undo removes the last stroke. Clear wipes the pad.

diff.q1: Can I compare two texts here?
diff.a1: Yes. Paste the original on the left and the new version on the right. The result marks added and removed lines.
diff.a2: It is a line-level comparison in this tab. It is not connected to Git and does not open files from a repo.
diff.a3: No. Comparison runs in this tab. Closing it discards both sides.
diff.a4: Yes. Ignore spaces collapses extra whitespace before comparing.
diff.a5: Yes. Copy puts a unified +/− listing on the clipboard.

uuid.q1: Can I generate a UUID here?
uuid.a1: Yes. It makes RFC 4122 version 4 UUIDs with Web Crypto in this tab.
uuid.q2: Are these sequential or based on MAC?
uuid.a2: No. Version 4 is random. There is no v1 time or hardware address.
uuid.a3: No. Random bytes come from Web Crypto locally. Closing the tab discards the list.
uuid.a4: Yes. Uncheck hyphens for a 32-character hex string. Uppercase is optional.
uuid.q5: Can I copy several at once?
uuid.a5: Yes. Copy list puts every UUID on its own line on the clipboard.

regex.q1: Can I test a regular expression here?
regex.a1: Yes. Type a pattern and sample text. Matches are listed in this tab.
regex.a2: No. The tester runs in this tab. Closing it discards the pattern and text.
regex.a3: g, i, m, s, and u. Sticky y is omitted. Invalid patterns show the engine error.
regex.a4: Yes. Fill replace to preview a substitution. $1 and $& work as in JavaScript.
regex.a5: Yes. Text is capped at 20,000 characters and 200 matches so the tab stays responsive.

favicon.q1: Can I make a favicon here?
favicon.a1: Yes. Drop a photo. The tab draws square PNG sizes and packs a .ico.
favicon.a2: No. Decoding and drawing stay in this tab. Closing it discards the image.
favicon.a3: 16, 32, and 48 pixel PNG images inside one favicon.ico file.
favicon.q4: Do you include Apple touch icons?
favicon.a4: The PNG zip has 180, 192, and 512 as well as the classic 16, 32, and 48 sizes.
favicon.q5: Can I keep a transparent background?
favicon.a5: Yes. Uncheck white background. Contain mode then letterboxes on transparency.

audio-cutter.a1: Yes. Drop a file, set start and end, then download a WAV of that slice.
audio-cutter.a2: No. Decoding and cutting stay in this tab. Closing it discards the audio.
audio-cutter.a3: Whatever this browser can decode: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, AAC, FLAC, or WebM. Output is always WAV.
audio-cutter.a4: Yes. Play selection plays from the start mark to the end mark.
audio-cutter.q5: Can I keep the original format?
audio-cutter.a5: No. The cut is written as WAV so the tab does not need an encoder for MP3 or AAC.

timestamp.q1: Can I convert a Unix timestamp here?
timestamp.a1: Yes. Paste seconds, milliseconds, or an ISO date. The tab shows UTC and your local time.
timestamp.q2: How do you tell seconds from milliseconds?
timestamp.a2: About 13 or more digits are milliseconds. Shorter numbers are seconds. ISO dates are parsed as dates.
timestamp.a3: No. Conversion runs in this tab. Closing it discards the input.
timestamp.a4: Now fills the current Unix time in seconds. A live line also shows the current second.
timestamp.a5: Yes. Copy puts seconds, milliseconds, ISO, and the UTC string on the clipboard.

rotate.q1: Can I rotate a photo here?
rotate.a1: Yes. Drop a photo, turn it 90° or any angle, flip it, then download.
rotate.a2: No. Decode, rotate, and export stay in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
rotate.a3: 90° and 180° keep the full photo. Other angles expand the canvas so nothing is clipped.
rotate.a4: Yes. Horizontal and vertical flips combine with the rotation angle.
rotate.a5: JPG, PNG, or WebP. JPG and WebP have a quality slider.

exif.a1: Yes. The tab re-encodes the photo, which drops EXIF, GPS, and similar tags.
exif.a2: No. Decode and export stay in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
exif.a3: Yes. Location tags live in EXIF. The new file is drawn without that block.
exif.a4: No. It writes a new picture without the original metadata tags. It is not a guarantee against every hidden channel.
exif.a5: JPG, PNG, or WebP. The new file comes from a canvas redraw.

audio-joiner.q1: Can I join audio files here?
audio-joiner.a1: Yes. Drop two or more clips, put them in order, then download one WAV.
audio-joiner.a2: No. Decoding and joining stay in this tab. Closing it discards the files.
audio-joiner.a3: Whatever this browser can decode: MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, AAC, FLAC, or WebM. Output is always WAV.
audio-joiner.a4: Later clips are resampled to the first clip’s rate before they are joined.
audio-joiner.a5: No. The joined file is WAV so the tab does not need an MP3 encoder.

hex-rgb.q1: Can I convert HEX to RGB here?
hex-rgb.a1: Yes. Paste #hex, rgb(), or hsl(). The tab shows RGB, HSL, and CMYK.
hex-rgb.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab. Closing it discards the color.
hex-rgb.a4: Yes. Copy puts HEX, rgb(), hsl(), and cmyk() on the clipboard.
hex-rgb.a5: The picker is a separate tool. This page is for converting values.

xml-json.q1: Can I convert XML to JSON here?
xml-json.a1: Yes. Paste XML for JSON, or JSON for XML. It runs in this tab.
xml-json.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab. Closing it discards both sides.
xml-json.a3: Attributes become keys prefixed with @. Text nodes use #text when mixed with children.
xml-json.a4: Simple documents do. Namespaces, mixed content, and DTDs are not a full XML suite.
xml-json.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted text on the clipboard.

hash.a1: Yes. MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 run in this tab.
hash.a2: No. Hashing stays in this tab. Closing it discards the input.
hash.a3: Yes. Open file reads it locally and hashes the bytes.
hash.a4: No. MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security. Use them for checksums, not password storage.

yaml-json.q1: Can I convert YAML to JSON here?
yaml-json.a1: Yes. Paste YAML for JSON, or JSON for YAML. It runs in this tab.
yaml-json.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab. Closing it discards both sides.
yaml-json.a3: Maps, lists, scalars, quotes, and simple inline [] {}. Anchors and tags are not a full YAML 1.2 suite.
yaml-json.a4: Simple configs do. Complex YAML (merge keys, custom tags) may not.
yaml-json.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted text on the clipboard.

case.q1: Can I change letter case here?
case.a1: Yes. Upper, lower, title, sentence, camel, Pascal, snake, kebab, and CONSTANT.
case.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab. Closing it discards the text.
case.q3: How does Title Case split words?
case.a3: It splits on spaces, punctuation, and camelCase boundaries.
case.a4: Basic Latin letters convert with toUpperCase/toLowerCase. Word splits keep common Latin letters.
case.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted text on the clipboard.

jwt.q1: Can I decode a JWT here?
jwt.a1: Yes. Paste a token. The tab shows the header and payload as JSON.
jwt.a2: No. Decoding stays in this tab. Closing it discards the token.
jwt.a3: No. This is a decoder only. It does not prove the token is authentic.
jwt.a4: If payload.exp is a Unix second, the tab says whether that time has passed.
jwt.a5: Yes. Copy puts the payload JSON on the clipboard.

screenshot.q1: Can I mark up a screenshot here?
screenshot.a1: Yes. Drop a photo, draw a box or arrow, add a label, then download a PNG.
screenshot.a2: No. Drawing stays in this tab. Closing it discards the file.
screenshot.a3: Rectangles, arrows, and text. Pick a color in the rail.
screenshot.a4: Yes. Undo removes the last mark.
screenshot.a5: A PNG of the photo plus the marks.

percent.q1: Can I calculate a percentage here?
percent.a1: Yes. Enter A and B. The tab shows A% of B, A as a percent of B, B plus A%, and the change from B to A.
percent.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
percent.a3: “What percent” and percent change are blank when the base is zero.
percent.a4: They use ordinary JavaScript numbers and are rounded for display.
percent.a5: Yes. Copy puts all four lines on the clipboard.

random.q1: Can I generate a random number here?
random.a1: Yes. Set min, max, and how many integers you want, then roll.
random.a2: No. Numbers come from crypto.getRandomValues in this tab.
random.a3: Yes. Both min and max can appear.
random.q4: How many numbers can I make?
random.a5: Yes. Copy puts one number per line.

html.a1: Yes. Paste text. Encode turns <>&"' into entities. Decode reverses named and numeric codes.
html.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
html.a3: amp, lt, gt, quot, apos, and nbsp. Other names stay as written. Numeric &#…; codes decode.
html.a4: No. This only rewrites characters. It does not execute HTML.
html.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted text on the clipboard.

cron.q1: Can I read a cron expression here?
cron.a1: Yes. Paste five fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.
cron.a2: No. Parsing stays in this tab.
cron.a3: No. Only the five numeric fields, *, ranges, lists, and */n steps.
cron.a5: No. It only explains the expression. It does not run jobs.

slug.q1: Can I make a URL slug here?
slug.a1: Yes. Paste a title. The tab lowercases it, drops accents, and joins words with hyphens.
slug.a2: No. The slug is built in this tab.
slug.q3: What happens to Chinese or emoji?
slug.a3: Characters that are not a–z or 0–9 become hyphens and then get trimmed.
slug.a4: It is capped at 80 characters, without a trailing hyphen.
slug.a5: Yes. Copy puts the slug on the clipboard.

portrait-sim.q1: Does this use my camera or upload photos?
portrait-sim.a1: No. Photoreal plates stay on cv.cm. Nothing is uploaded. Snap downloads stay on your device. Your camera is not used.
portrait-sim.q2: Why doesn’t UV change the picture?
portrait-sim.a2: Digital sensors already block UV. A UV filter is nearly clear. It is not a UV lens. ND, polarizer and diffusion are the filters you can see.
portrait-sim.q3: Can I try a phone lens?
portrait-sim.a3: Yes. Choose Phone 26 mm-e. Aperture stays at f/1.8 because a phone iris is fixed.
portrait-sim.q4: Is this studio lighting or a moving key light?
portrait-sim.a4: Scene exposure is white balance on a pre-lit plate. Fill light (white, blacklight, gold) is a gel on the sitter, not a moving key.
portrait-sim.q5: Are the people real, or children?
portrait-sim.a5: They are simulated adult sitters only — photoreal and anime. There are no minors and no uploads of real faces.

age.a1: Yes. Pick a birth date and a date. The tab shows years, months, days, and total days.
age.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
age.a3: Civil months: if the day has not been reached, the previous month is used.
age.a4: February 29 is a real date. The next years count from the civil calendar.
age.a5: Yes. Copy puts a one-line summary on the clipboard.

bmi.a1: Yes. Enter kilograms and centimetres. The tab shows BMI and a WHO band.
bmi.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
bmi.a3: Under 18.5, 18.5–24.9, 25–29.9, and 30+ as used by WHO adult BMI.
bmi.a4: No. It is a simple index. It is not medical advice.
bmi.a5: Yes. Copy puts the BMI and band on the clipboard.

binary.q1: Can I convert text to binary here?
binary.a1: Yes. Text becomes 8-bit UTF-8 groups. Binary can be turned back into text.
binary.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
binary.a3: Spaces are ignored when decoding. Encoding puts a space between bytes.
binary.q4: What if the bits are not a multiple of 8?
binary.a4: Decode fails. Each UTF-8 byte needs eight 0/1 digits.
binary.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted text on the clipboard.

tip.q1: Can I calculate a tip here?
tip.a1: Yes. Enter the bill, a percent, and how many people. The tab shows the tip, total, and share.
tip.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
tip.a3: The people count is a whole number of 1 or more. The share is the total divided by that count.
tip.a4: None. It is just a number with two decimal places.
tip.a5: Yes. Copy puts tip, total, and per person on the clipboard.

morse.a1: Yes. Text becomes dots and dashes. Morse can be turned back into letters.
morse.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
morse.a3: Letters are spaced. Words use a slash. Unknown Morse returns an error.
morse.a4: International Morse for Latin letters, digits, and a few punctuation marks.
morse.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted text on the clipboard.

roman.q1: Can I convert Roman numerals here?
roman.a1: Yes. Numbers 1 to 3999 become standard subtractive Roman, and valid Roman becomes a number.
roman.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
roman.a3: This tab uses the common form IV for 4. Additive IIII is rejected.
roman.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted value on the clipboard.

discount.q1: Can I calculate a discount here?
discount.a1: Yes. Enter the original price and a percent off. The tab shows the sale price and how much you save.
discount.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
discount.a3: Yes. A 120% off price can go negative. That is still just arithmetic.
discount.a4: None. It is just a number with two decimal places.
discount.a5: Yes. Copy puts sale price and savings on the clipboard.

countdown.q1: Can I run a countdown here?
countdown.a1: Yes. Set hours, minutes, and seconds, then start. Pause and reset are in this tab.
countdown.a2: No. The timer runs in this tab. Closing it stops the count.
countdown.q3: Does it keep running in the background?
countdown.a3: Only while this tab stays open. It is not a system alarm.
countdown.q5: Can I change the time while it runs?
countdown.a5: Pause or reset, then edit the fields.

loan.q1: Can I estimate a loan payment here?
loan.a1: Yes. Enter principal, yearly interest percent, and years. The tab shows a fixed monthly payment.
loan.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
loan.a3: A standard amortizing payment: n is months, r is yearly rate / 12.
loan.a4: No. Fees, compounding, and extra payments are not included.
loan.a5: Yes. Copy puts payment, total interest, and total paid on the clipboard.

stopwatch.a1: Yes. Start, pause, and reset a stopwatch in this tab. It shows hours, minutes, seconds, and hundredths.
stopwatch.a2: No. The timer runs in this tab.
stopwatch.q3: Does it keep running in the background?
stopwatch.a3: Only while this tab stays open. Closing the tab stops it. It is not a system clock.
stopwatch.a4: The display is hundredths of a second. It is for elapsed time, not a certified lab timer.
stopwatch.a5: No. This tab only tracks total elapsed time.

compound.q1: Can I calculate compound interest here?
compound.a1: Yes. Enter principal, yearly percent, years, and how often it compounds. The tab shows future value and interest earned.
compound.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
compound.a3: A = P (1 + r/n)^(n t). n is compounds per year. Yearly, quarterly, monthly, and daily are built in.
compound.a4: No. Fees, inflation, and taxes are not included.
compound.a5: None. It is just a number with two decimal places.

vat.q1: Can I calculate VAT or sales tax here?
vat.a1: Yes. Enter an amount and a rate. Exclusive adds tax. Inclusive splits a gross price into net and tax.
vat.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
vat.a3: The rate you enter. This tab does not look up a country rate.
vat.a4: No. It is arithmetic on the numbers you type.
vat.a5: None. It is just a number with two decimal places.

games.q1: Can I play NES games in the browser?
games.a1: Yes. NES through Mega Drive use EmulatorJS from GitHub (fceumm, snes9x, gambatte, mGBA, Genesis Plus GX). Cores are on S3. Flash opens a SWF with Ruffle. Touch controls work on phones.
games.q2: Do you host Super Mario or Contra ROMs?
games.a2: No commercial dumps. Those pages have cheats and walkthroughs; you load a ROM you own. Shiru freeware (Alter Ego, Lawn Mower) starts without a file.
games.a3: Each game page lists Game Genie / Gameshark-style codes. After the ROM boots, paste them in the emulator cheat menu. Codes depend on the dump version.
games.a4: No. A local file is read in this tab and handed to the emulator. Homebrew we may redistribute is fetched from our S3 bucket.
games.q5: Which consoles work on a phone?
games.a5: NES, GB, GBC, and most GBA / Mega Drive titles. SNES is heavier. Flash plays a SWF you choose, with touch treated as the mouse. Landscape plus a Bluetooth pad helps fighters and karts.

reverse.a1: Yes. Paste text and the tab shows it backwards. It also says whether the letters and digits form a palindrome.
reverse.a2: No. The text stays in this tab.
reverse.a3: Yes. Spaces, punctuation, and letter case are ignored. “Race car” counts as a palindrome.
reverse.a4: Graphemes reverse in order. Palindrome uses letters and digits, including CJK characters.
reverse.a5: Yes. Copy puts the reversed text on the clipboard.

url-encode.a1: Yes. Encode uses percent-encoding (encodeURIComponent). Decode turns % sequences back into text.
url-encode.a2: No. Encoding stays in this tab.
url-encode.a3: On decode, + becomes a space, like query strings often do.
url-encode.q4: Is this a full URL parser?
url-encode.a4: No. It encodes or decodes the string you paste. It does not split a URL into parts.
url-encode.a5: A broken % sequence shows an error. Fix the hex pairs and try again.

text-hex.q1: Can I convert text to hex here?
text-hex.a1: Yes. Text becomes UTF-8 bytes as two-digit hex. Hex can convert back to text.
text-hex.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
text-hex.a3: Spaces, colons, and 0x prefixes are ignored on decode. Odd-length hex is invalid.
text-hex.a4: UTF-8. Invalid UTF-8 bytes return an error.
text-hex.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted value on the clipboard.

json.a1: Yes. Paste JSON and pretty-print it with indent, or minify it to one line.
json.a2: No. Formatting stays in this tab.
json.q3: What if the JSON is invalid?
json.a3: The tab shows an error. Trailing commas and comments are not JSON.
json.q4: Is this the same as Text and data?
json.a4: Text and data also formats JSON. This page is only pretty-print and minify.
json.a5: Yes. Copy puts the formatted JSON on the clipboard.

base64.a1: Yes. Encode text as Base64, or decode Base64 back to text. UTF-8 is used.
base64.a2: No. Encoding stays in this tab.
base64.a3: This tab is for text. It is not a file host.
base64.a4: Padding must be valid Base64. Broken input shows an error.
base64.a5: Yes. Copy puts the encoded or decoded string on the clipboard.

days.q1: Can I count days between two dates here?
days.a1: Yes. Pick a start date and an end date. The tab shows the signed day count, the absolute days, and whole weeks.
days.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
days.a3: No. These are civil calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD), not clock times.
days.a4: Yes. 28 Feb 2024 to 1 Mar 2024 is 2 days.
days.a5: Yes. Copy puts the day counts on the clipboard.

sort.a1: Yes. Paste one item per line. Sort A→Z, Z→A, or keep the first copy of each line.
sort.a2: No. Sorting stays in this tab.
sort.a3: No. Unique keeps the first time a line appears, in the original order.
sort.a4: Yes. Uppercase letters sort before lowercase in Unicode order.
sort.a5: Yes. Copy puts the lines on the clipboard.

replace.q1: Can I find and replace text here?
replace.a1: Yes. Enter the find string and the replacement. Replace all matches or only the first.
replace.a2: No. Replacement stays in this tab.
replace.a3: No. It is literal text. Use the regex tester if you need patterns.
replace.a4: Nothing changes. An empty find is ignored.
replace.a5: Yes. Copy puts the replaced text on the clipboard.

words.q1: Can I turn a number into words here?
words.a1: Yes. Whole numbers from 0 to 999,999,999,999 become US English words.
words.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
words.a3: No. 101 is “one hundred one”, not “one hundred and one”.
words.a4: No. Only whole numbers from 0 up.
words.a5: Yes. Copy puts the words on the clipboard.

add-days.q1: Can I add days to a date here?
add-days.a1: Yes. Pick a date and a whole number of days. Negative numbers go backwards.
add-days.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
add-days.a3: Yes. 28 Feb 2024 plus 1 day is 29 Feb 2024.
add-days.a4: No. These are civil calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD), not clock times.
add-days.a5: Yes. Copy puts the new date on the clipboard.

week.q1: Can I find the week number here?
week.a1: Yes. Pick a date. The tab shows the ISO week, ISO year, and weekday. Monday is day 1.
week.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
week.a3: No. This is ISO-8601. Week 1 is the week with the year’s first Thursday. A late December date can belong to the next year’s week 1.
week.a4: Sunday is weekday 7. The ISO week still starts on Monday.
week.a5: Yes. Copy puts the ISO week label and weekday on the clipboard.

aspect.q1: Can I get an aspect ratio here?
aspect.a1: Yes. Enter width and height in pixels. The tab simplifies them, like 1920×1080 → 16:9.
aspect.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
aspect.a3: No. It only reduces the two numbers. Use Crop if you need to cut a picture.
aspect.a4: Width and height are rounded to whole pixels before simplifying.
aspect.a5: Yes. Copy puts the ratio, such as 16:9, on the clipboard.

workdays.q1: Can I count business days here?
workdays.a1: Yes. Pick two dates. The tab counts Monday through Friday and includes both dates when they are weekdays.
workdays.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
workdays.a3: No. Only Saturdays and Sundays are skipped. Local holidays stay in the count.
workdays.q4: What if both dates are the same?
workdays.a4: A weekday counts as 1. A Saturday or Sunday counts as 0.
workdays.a5: Yes. Copy puts the business-day count and the weekend days on the clipboard.

fraction.q1: Can I simplify a fraction here?
fraction.a1: Yes. Enter a whole numerator and denominator, or switch to a decimal. 4/6 becomes 2/3. 0.75 becomes 3/4.
fraction.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
fraction.a3: No. Results are improper or whole, such as 5/2 or 3, not 2 1/2.
fraction.q4: How close is a repeating decimal?
fraction.a4: Decimals use a continued fraction with a denominator up to 10,000. 0.333333 becomes 1/3.
fraction.a5: Yes. Copy puts the simplified fraction, such as 2/3, on the clipboard.

hourly.q1: Can I turn hourly pay into a yearly salary?
hourly.a1: Yes. Enter an hourly wage, hours per week, and weeks per year. Switch the mode to start from a yearly amount.
hourly.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
hourly.a3: No. This is gross pay only. It does not subtract tax, insurance, or overtime premiums.
hourly.a4: 40 hours a week and 52 weeks a year, which is 2,080 hours. Change either number if your year is shorter.
hourly.a5: Yes. Copy puts hourly, weekly, and yearly gross pay on the clipboard.

margin.q1: Can I calculate a profit margin here?
margin.a1: Yes. Enter a cost and a selling price. The tab shows profit, margin, and markup.
margin.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
margin.q3: What is the difference between margin and markup?
margin.a3: Margin is profit divided by the selling price. Markup is profit divided by the cost. Cost 50 and price 80 is 30 profit, a 37.50% margin, and a 60% markup.
margin.q4: What if the price is below the cost?
margin.a4: Profit, margin, and markup are negative. A zero price has no margin percent. A zero cost has no markup percent.
margin.a5: Yes. Copy puts profit, margin, and markup on the clipboard.

radix.q1: Can I convert binary, decimal, and hex here?
radix.a1: Yes. Type a whole number and two bases from 2 to 36. 255 in base 10 becomes FF in base 16.
radix.a2: No. Conversion stays in this tab.
radix.a3: No. This converts one integer. The binary tool turns letters into groups of 8 bits.
radix.q4: Can I use a 0x prefix or a fraction?
radix.a4: No. Do not type 0x or 0b, and do not type a decimal point. A digit must exist in the source base, so 2 is not a binary digit.
radix.a5: Yes. Copy puts the converted integer on the clipboard. Letters are uppercase.

duration.q1: Can I add hours and minutes here?
duration.a1: Yes. Enter two durations as hours:minutes:seconds. Add them, or subtract the second from the first.
duration.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
duration.q3: What format do the times use?
duration.a3: Use H:MM:SS, such as 1:30:00. Minutes and seconds must be from 0 to 59.
duration.q4: What if the second time is longer?
duration.a4: Subtracting a longer duration gives a negative result, such as -0:15:00. This is a length of time, not a clock or a time zone.
duration.a5: Yes. Copy puts the duration and the total seconds on the clipboard.

tdee.q1: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
tdee.a1: BMR is what your body burns at complete rest. TDEE multiplies it by an activity factor from 1.2 (desk job, little exercise) to 1.9 (hard training every day), so it is the rough number of calories that keeps your weight steady.
tdee.a2: Mifflin–St Jeor: 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age, plus 5 for men or minus 161 for women. It is the equation most dietitians reach for first, but any formula is an estimate.
tdee.q3: Where do the cut and bulk numbers come from?
tdee.a3: Cut is TDEE minus 500 kcal a day, which is roughly 0.5 kg (1 lb) a week. Bulk is TDEE plus 300 kcal for a slow gain. Watch the scale for two or three weeks and adjust. It never goes below your BMR or 1,200 kcal (women) / 1,500 kcal (men); the page says when that limit applies.
tdee.a4: No. It is an estimate for healthy adults. If you are pregnant, under 18, have a medical condition or want to lose weight fast, talk to a doctor or dietitian.
tdee.a5: No. Age, height and weight stay in this tab and are not saved.

cidr.a1: The number after the slash is how many leading bits are the network. /24 leaves 8 bits for hosts: 256 addresses, mask 255.255.255.0.
cidr.q2: Why are usable hosts two fewer than the total?
cidr.a2: The first address is the network and the last is the broadcast, so a normal subnet cannot give them to hosts. /31 is the exception (two usable, for point-to-point links, RFC 3021) and /32 is a single host.
cidr.q3: Can I type a netmask instead of a prefix?
cidr.a3: Yes. Type an address and a mask with a space, such as 10.1.2.3 255.255.252.0. A bare address is read as /32.
cidr.q4: What does the range to CIDR box do?
cidr.a4: It covers a start and end address with the fewest CIDR blocks. 10.0.0.5 to 10.0.0.20 becomes 10.0.0.5/32, 10.0.0.6/31, 10.0.0.8/29, 10.0.0.16/30 and 10.0.0.20/32.
cidr.q5: Does it support IPv6 or send my addresses anywhere?
cidr.a5: IPv4 only for now. Everything is calculated in this tab; nothing is sent.

chmod.a1: Each digit is one group: owner, group, others. Read is 4, write 2, execute 1. 7 = rwx for the owner, 5 = r-x for the group and for everyone else: rwxr-xr-x.
chmod.q2: What are setuid, setgid and the sticky bit?
chmod.a2: They are the optional fourth (leading) digit. Setuid (4) runs a program as its owner, setgid (2) runs it as its group or makes new files in a folder inherit the group, and sticky (1) on a folder such as /tmp lets only a file's owner delete it.
chmod.q3: Why do I see a capital S or T?
chmod.a3: ls shows s or t when the special bit and execute are both set, and S or T when the special bit is set without execute, which is usually a mistake.
chmod.q4: Can I paste the string from ls -l?
chmod.a4: Yes. Paste rwxr-xr-x or the full -rwxr-xr-x (the first letter is the file type and is ignored) and the boxes and octal update.
chmod.a5: No. It only builds the command. Copy it and run it in your own terminal.

typing.a1: Net WPM counts only correctly typed characters, divides by 5 (the standard word length) and then by the minutes used. Wrong characters lower accuracy and add nothing to speed.
typing.q2: Why does Chinese, Japanese or Korean show characters per minute?
typing.a2: Those languages are not split into words by spaces and are typed through an input method, so a WPM figure would be invented. We count correct characters per minute, not counting spaces.
typing.a3: With your first keystroke. The test stops when time runs out or you finish the passage, whichever comes first.
typing.a4: No. Paste and drop are turned off in the typing box so the result reflects real typing.
typing.q5: Are my results saved or sent?
typing.a5: No. The score is shown on this page only. Reloading clears it.

image-colors.q1: How does it pick the colors?
image-colors.a1: It shrinks a copy of the image, groups similar pixels with median cut, then refines the groups with a few rounds of k-means. Each color shows its share of the picture.
image-colors.a2: No. The file is decoded and analysed in this tab with a canvas. Nothing is sent and analytics are off on this page.
image-colors.q3: How many colors can I get?
image-colors.a3: From 2 to 12. A flat logo may return fewer, because identical colors are merged.
image-colors.q4: How do I copy a color?
image-colors.a4: Click a swatch to copy its HEX code, or use Copy all for the whole palette, one code per line.
image-colors.a5: No. Pixels that are more than half transparent are skipped, so a PNG cut-out gives the colors of the subject.

heic-to-jpg.q1: Can I convert HEIC to JPG here?
heic-to-jpg.a1: Yes, in Safari and Chrome. Drop the photo and download a JPG. Nothing is uploaded.
heic-to-jpg.a2: This browser cannot decode HEIC. Use Safari or Chrome. Firefox on Windows often fails.
heic-to-jpg.q3: Does converting make the photo sharper?
heic-to-jpg.a3: No. It only changes the format so more programs can open it. Keep the HEIC if you still edit on iPhone.
heic-to-jpg.q4: Can I convert several HEIC files?
heic-to-jpg.a4: Yes. Drop a batch and download a ZIP of JPGs.
heic-to-jpg.a5: JPG never has transparency. A clear area becomes a solid background.

webp-to-png.q1: Can I convert WebP to PNG?
webp-to-png.a1: Yes. Drop the WebP and download a PNG. Nothing is uploaded.
webp-to-png.a2: Yes, if you export PNG. JPG fills clear pixels, often with black.
webp-to-png.a3: Some forms, editors, and older apps open PNG and reject WebP.
webp-to-png.q4: Can I convert a batch of WebP files?
webp-to-png.a4: Yes. Download one file or a ZIP.
webp-to-png.a5: Usually not. PNG is the compatible copy. Use WebP or JPG when size matters more than a clear edge.

png-to-jpg.q1: Can I convert PNG to JPG?
png-to-jpg.a1: Yes. Drop the PNG and download a JPG. Nothing is uploaded.
png-to-jpg.q2: Why did the background turn black?
png-to-jpg.a2: JPG cannot store transparency. Clear pixels are filled. Use PNG if the edge must stay clear.
png-to-jpg.a3: Photo PNGs usually shrink. A tiny flat graphic may not.
png-to-jpg.a4: Yes. Download one file or a ZIP.
png-to-jpg.a5: No. JPG is a smaller compatible copy, not a sharper one.

jpg-to-png.q1: Can I convert JPG to PNG?
jpg-to-png.a1: Yes. Drop the JPG and download a PNG. Nothing is uploaded.
jpg-to-png.a2: No. JPG has no transparency to recover. The PNG is a solid picture.
jpg-to-png.a3: PNG is lossless. A photo that was JPEG-compressed usually grows.
jpg-to-png.a4: When the next app rejects JPG, or you will edit without another JPEG save.
jpg-to-png.q5: Can I convert a batch of JPGs?
jpg-to-png.a5: Yes. Download one file or a ZIP.

avif-to-jpg.q1: Can I convert AVIF to JPG?
avif-to-jpg.a1: Yes, in a browser that can decode AVIF. Download a JPG. Nothing is uploaded.
avif-to-jpg.q2: Why is the AVIF preview blank?
avif-to-jpg.a2: This browser cannot read AVIF. Use a current Chrome, Edge, or Safari.
avif-to-jpg.q3: Does this make the photo sharper?
avif-to-jpg.a3: No. It only changes the format. Keep the AVIF if you still edit it.
avif-to-jpg.q4: Can I convert several AVIF files?
avif-to-jpg.a4: Yes. Drop a batch and download a ZIP of JPGs.
avif-to-jpg.q5: Will a chat app open the JPG?
avif-to-jpg.a5: JPG is the format older mail, print, and chat apps expect.

png-to-webp.q1: Can I convert PNG to WebP?
png-to-webp.a1: Yes. Drop the PNG and download a WebP. Nothing is uploaded.
png-to-webp.a2: Yes. Unlike JPG, WebP can keep a clear edge.
png-to-webp.q3: Why would I stay with PNG?
png-to-webp.a3: An old form, email client, or editor may reject WebP. Send PNG there.
png-to-webp.a4: Usually for photos and large graphics. Compare the download size before you replace the original.
png-to-webp.q5: Can I convert a batch to WebP?
png-to-webp.a5: Yes. Download one file or a ZIP.

compress-image.q1: Can I compress an image here?
compress-image.a1: Yes. Drop a photo, lower the quality, and download a smaller JPG or WebP. Nothing is uploaded.
compress-image.q2: How do I reduce image size?
compress-image.a2: Use a lower quality, or the 1920, 1280, or 800 preset when the pixel size is the problem. Read the size line before you download.
compress-image.a3: Screen-size photos can take a lower quality and still look fine. If text turns mushy, raise the quality.
compress-image.a4: PNG does not use the quality slider. Export JPG or WebP when you need a smaller file.
compress-image.a5: No. You download a new file. The one on disk stays as it was.

gold.q1: Is a troy ounce the ounce in the unit tool?
gold.a1: No. A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams. The unit tool's oz is the avoirdupois ounce, about 28.35 grams.
gold.a2: The Hong Kong gold tael is 37.429 grams. The market tael is 50 grams. The Taiwan tael is 37.5 grams.
gold.q3: Why is there no gold price?
gold.a3: This page only uses numbers you type. It does not fetch or prefill a price.
gold.q4: What if the price box is empty?
gold.a4: You only see the five weights. Prices appear after you type US dollars per troy ounce.
gold.q5: Can I place an order from this?
gold.a5: No. This is a conversion, not investment advice and not a quote.

silver.q1: Is a troy ounce the ounce in the unit tool?
silver.a1: No. A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams. The unit tool's oz is the avoirdupois ounce, about 28.35 grams.
silver.a2: The Hong Kong gold tael is 37.429 grams. The market tael is 50 grams. The Taiwan tael is 37.5 grams.
silver.q3: Why is there no silver price?
silver.a3: This page only uses numbers you type. It does not fetch or prefill a price.
silver.q4: What if the price box is empty?
silver.a4: You only see the five weights. Prices appear after you type US dollars per troy ounce.
silver.q5: Can I place an order from this?
silver.a5: No. This is a conversion, not investment advice and not a quote.

platinum.q1: Is a troy ounce the ounce in the unit tool?
platinum.a1: No. A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams. The unit tool's oz is the avoirdupois ounce, about 28.35 grams.
platinum.a2: The Hong Kong gold tael is 37.429 grams. The market tael is 50 grams. The Taiwan tael is 37.5 grams.
platinum.q3: Why is there no platinum price?
platinum.a3: This page only uses numbers you type. It does not fetch or prefill a price.
platinum.q4: What if the price box is empty?
platinum.a4: You only see the five weights. Prices appear after you type US dollars per troy ounce.
platinum.q5: Can I place an order from this?
platinum.a5: No. This is a conversion, not investment advice and not a quote.

palladium.q1: Is a troy ounce the ounce in the unit tool?
palladium.a1: No. A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams. The unit tool's oz is the avoirdupois ounce, about 28.35 grams.
palladium.a2: The Hong Kong gold tael is 37.429 grams. The market tael is 50 grams. The Taiwan tael is 37.5 grams.
palladium.q3: Why is there no palladium price?
palladium.a3: This page only uses numbers you type. It does not fetch or prefill a price.
palladium.q4: What if the price box is empty?
palladium.a4: You only see the five weights. Prices appear after you type US dollars per troy ounce.
palladium.q5: Can I place an order from this?
palladium.a5: No. This is a conversion, not investment advice and not a quote.

oil.q1: How many liters are in an oil barrel?
oil.a1: One petroleum barrel is 42 US gallons, which is 158.987294928 liters.
oil.a2: No. The conversion stays in this tab.
oil.q3: Is a US gallon the same as a litre bottle?
oil.a3: A US gallon is 3.785411784 liters. It is not an imperial gallon.
oil.q4: Why is there no oil price?
oil.a4: This page only converts volume. It does not fetch a price.
oil.a5: Yes. Copy puts barrels, gallons, and liters on the clipboard.

stocks.q1: Which share count does market cap use?
stocks.a1: Company market cap is price times shares outstanding. Do not type the shares in your account.
stocks.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
stocks.q3: What if earnings per share are zero?
stocks.a3: P/E stays blank. The page does not show infinity.
stocks.q4: What if the price is zero?
stocks.a4: Dividend yield stays blank because the divisor is zero.
stocks.q5: Does this page show a stock price?
stocks.a5: No. You type the price. It is arithmetic, not a recommendation.

gamesFlash.q1: Can I play Flash games in the browser?
gamesFlash.a1: Yes. This page runs SWF files with Ruffle, an open-source Flash emulator. You do not install Adobe Flash Player.
gamesFlash.q2: What if there is no game file?
gamesFlash.a2: The player says to upload one. Choose a SWF. The file stays in this tab and is not sent to a server.
gamesFlash.q3: Why does a SWF fail to start?
gamesFlash.a3: Many games are more than one file, or they only run on the original website. This page is for a single SWF that can run alone. Some ActionScript 3 games are still incomplete.
gamesFlash.q4: Does Flash work on a phone?
gamesFlash.a4: It opens. Touch is treated as the mouse. Games that need hover or a keyboard are easier on a computer.
gamesFlash.q5: Can I download classic Flash games here?
gamesFlash.a5: No. Use a SWF you already have. cv.cm will only host a SWF when its license allows redistribution.

mosaic.a1: No. The photo stays in this tab. The canvas replaces the pixels here. Closing the tab discards it. Export also strips EXIF.
mosaic.a2: Use a black box for ID numbers, card numbers, and QR codes. A fine mosaic can sometimes be guessed back. Use mosaic for faces and background clutter.
mosaic.q3: Can I redact a chat screenshot?
mosaic.a3: Yes. Drop the screenshot and drag over avatars, names, and phone numbers. Draw as many boxes as you need; Undo removes the last one. With several photos, each keeps its own boxes and you can download a ZIP.
mosaic.q4: Can I add a watermark after redacting?
mosaic.a4: Yes. On the same page, add a “for [org] use only” mark. Redaction is applied first, then the mark.
mosaic.a5: No. This only covers areas. It cannot restore pixels someone else covered. In your export the covered pixels are replaced, not hidden.

dice.a1: Yes. Pick how many dice and which die, then press Roll. Each face and the total appear on the right.
dice.a2: No. The rolls happen in this tab.
dice.a3: d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, and d100, up to 50 dice at once. 2d6 means two six-sided dice.
dice.a4: Each roll uses the browser's cryptographic random generator, so every face has the same chance. Nothing is seeded or stored.
dice.a5: Yes. Set a number of coins and press Flip. The tab shows each face and the heads and tails counts.

gpa.q1: Can I calculate my GPA here?
gpa.a1: Yes. Pick a letter grade and credits for each course. The GPA updates as you type.
gpa.a2: No. The math stays in this tab.
gpa.a3: Each grade becomes points: A 4.0, A- 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, down to F 0. Points times credits are added up and divided by the total credits.
gpa.a4: By default A+ is 4.0. Tick A+ = 4.3 if your school uses that scale.
gpa.a5: A course with 0 or blank credits is skipped. Pass/fail courses usually do not count toward GPA.

pomodoro.q1: Can I run a Pomodoro timer here?
pomodoro.a1: Yes. Press Start. The tab counts down a focus session, chimes, and moves to a break by itself.
pomodoro.a2: No. The timer runs in this tab. Nothing is sent or stored.
pomodoro.a3: Work in focused blocks, usually 25 minutes, then rest 5 minutes. After four blocks take a longer 15-minute break. Each block is one pomodoro.
pomodoro.a4: Yes. Set focus, short break, and long break in minutes from 1 to 180, and the number of rounds before a long break. While the clock is stopped the current phase takes the new length right away; Reset starts over from round 1.
pomodoro.q5: What happens if I switch tabs?
pomodoro.a5: The timer keeps counting from the clock, and the tab title shows the time left. Keep the tab open to hear the chime.

sleep.q1: How does the sleep calculator work?
sleep.a1: Sleep runs in cycles of about 90 minutes. The tool counts back from your wake-up time (or forward from your bedtime) in whole cycles and adds about 14 minutes to fall asleep, so an alarm lands at the end of a cycle instead of in deep sleep.
sleep.a2: No. The times are computed in this tab and nothing is sent or stored.
sleep.q3: How many cycles should I sleep?
sleep.a3: Five or six cycles (7.5 to 9 hours) suit most adults. Three or four cycles are shown for short nights; use them when you must, not every night.
sleep.a4: Most people take 10 to 20 minutes to fall asleep. The calculator uses 14 minutes as an average; if you drop off faster or slower, shift the result by the difference.
sleep.a5: No. Cycles range from about 70 to 120 minutes and change through the night, so treat the times as a starting point and adjust by how you feel on waking.

body-fat.q1: How is body fat estimated here?
body-fat.a1: With the U.S. Navy circumference method: height, neck and waist for men, plus hips for women, go into a logarithmic formula. Add weight to split the result into fat mass and lean mass.
body-fat.a2: No. The measurements stay in this tab and are not stored.
body-fat.a3: Neck just below the larynx, tape sloping slightly down to the front. Waist at the navel for men and at the narrowest point for women. Hips at the widest point. Keep the tape snug but not tight.
body-fat.a4: Usually within 3 to 4 percentage points of a DEXA scan for most adults, less for very muscular or very lean people. Measure in the morning and repeat the same way to track change over time.
body-fat.a5: The ACE ranges: for men essential 2–5%, athletes 6–13%, fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%, obese 25%+; for women essential 10–13%, athletes 14–20%, fitness 21–24%, average 25–31%, obese 32%+.

contrast.q1: What does the contrast ratio mean?
contrast.a1: It compares the relative luminance of the text color and the background on a scale from 1:1 (same color) to 21:1 (black on white), as defined by WCAG 2.
contrast.a2: No. The ratio is computed in this tab.
contrast.a3: WCAG AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; AAA asks for 7:1 and 4.5:1. Icons, borders and form controls need 3:1 (non-text contrast).
contrast.a5: When the pair fails AA for normal text, the text color is moved step by step toward black or white, whichever helps, until it reaches 4.5:1. Hue is kept as close as possible.

pace.q1: How do I use the pace calculator?
pace.a1: Pick what to solve for, choose km or miles, and fill in the other two values. Time accepts h:mm:ss or mm:ss; pace accepts m:ss.
pace.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
pace.a3: Finish times for 5K, 10K, half marathon (21.0975 km) and marathon (42.195 km) if you held the same pace the whole way. Real race times slow down over longer distances.
pace.q4: How do I convert pace per km to pace per mile?
pace.a4: Multiply by 1.609. The result shows both: 5:00 /km is about 8:03 /mi.
pace.a5: Yes. Speed in km/h or mph is shown next to the pace, so 12 km/h equals a 5:00 /km pace.

grade.q1: How is the needed score calculated?
grade.a1: Needed = (wanted − current × (1 − weight)) ÷ weight, with the weight of the final as a fraction. With 85% now, a 90% goal and a 30% final you need 101.7%.
grade.a2: No. The numbers stay in this tab.
grade.q3: What if the result is over 100%?
grade.a3: The goal is out of reach on the final alone unless there is extra credit. Check the table for the highest letter that is still possible.
grade.q4: What if the result is 0% or less?
grade.a4: You already have the grade you want. Any score on the final keeps it.
grade.a5: Your average on everything graded so far, as a percentage, before the final. If your syllabus lists category weights, use the weighted average your gradebook shows.

due-date.q1: How is the due date calculated?
due-date.a1: With Naegele's rule: 280 days (40 weeks) after the first day of the last period for a 28-day cycle. A longer or shorter cycle shifts the date by the difference, so a 32-day cycle adds 4 days.
due-date.a2: No. The dates are computed in this tab and nothing is stored.
due-date.q3: What if I know the conception date instead?
due-date.a3: Pick Conception date. The due date is 266 days after it. If you already have a due date from a scan, pick Due date to see the weeks and trimesters.
due-date.a4: Only about 4% of babies arrive on the due date; most come within two weeks either side. An early ultrasound gives the most reliable date and overrides this estimate.
due-date.a5: The second trimester starts at 13 weeks + 0 days and the third at 27 weeks + 0 days, counted from the last period. Different books use slightly different cut-offs.

ideal-weight.a1: Devine (1974), Robinson (1983), Miller (1983) and Hamwi (1964). Each gives a base weight at 5 feet and adds a fixed amount per inch above it, with separate numbers for men and women.
ideal-weight.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
ideal-weight.a3: They were fitted to different groups, mostly for drug dosing and insurance tables, so they differ by a few kilograms. Treat the spread as the range, not any single number as the target.
ideal-weight.q4: What is the BMI range row?
ideal-weight.a4: The weights that give a BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 at your height, the WHO healthy range for adults. It does not account for muscle mass or age.
ideal-weight.a5: The formulas are defined from 5 feet (152.4 cm) upward; below that the tool extrapolates the same per-inch step down to 140 cm, so treat those results as rough.

water-intake.a1: About 35 ml per kilogram of body weight, plus about 12 ml per minute of exercise, plus 500 ml in hot or humid weather. A 70 kg person with 30 minutes of exercise gets about 2.8 litres.
water-intake.a2: No. The numbers stay in this tab.
water-intake.q3: Does the total include food and other drinks?
water-intake.a3: It is total fluid. Roughly a fifth usually comes from food, and tea, coffee and milk count toward it.
water-intake.a4: No. It is a rule of thumb for healthy adults. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, kidney or heart conditions and some medicines change the need; ask a doctor.
water-intake.a5: 250 ml, about 8.5 US fluid ounces. The glass count is rounded up.

fuel-cost.q1: How is the fuel cost calculated?
fuel-cost.a1: Distance is turned into litres with your car's economy, then multiplied by the price per litre. 300 km at 7 L/100 km uses 21 litres; at 1.60 a litre that is 33.60.
fuel-cost.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
fuel-cost.a3: L/100 km, km/L and US mpg. Price can be per litre or per US gallon; the tool converts between them.
fuel-cost.q4: How do I split the cost?
fuel-cost.a4: Enter the number of people. Cost per person divides the total evenly, including the driver.
fuel-cost.q5: Why is the real cost higher?
fuel-cost.a5: Economy figures are for mixed driving; city traffic, air conditioning, roof racks and a loaded car use more. Add about 10% for a safe estimate.

reading-time.a1: Words divided by a reading speed: 150 words a minute for slow, 238 for average adult silent reading, 300 for fast. Speaking time uses 130 words a minute.
reading-time.a2: No. The text stays in this tab.
reading-time.q3: How are Chinese, Japanese and Korean counted?
reading-time.a3: In characters, not words: 200, 300 or 400 characters a minute for reading and 180 for speaking. Mixed text counts Latin words and CJK characters separately.
reading-time.q4: Is the average speed right for me?
reading-time.a4: 238 words a minute is the mean for adults reading non-fiction in English (Brysbaert, 2019). Technical text is slower; pick Slow for it.
reading-time.q5: Can I use it for a speech?
reading-time.a5: Yes. The speaking row uses a conversational 130 words a minute. Presenters often speak 110–150, so adjust by a minute or two for pauses.

time-card.a1: For each shift, end time minus start time minus the unpaid break. 09:00 to 17:30 with a 30-minute break is 8 hours. The week's shifts are added up.
time-card.a2: No. The times stay in this tab and are not stored.
time-card.a3: Yes. If the end time is earlier than the start, the shift runs past midnight: 22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours. A moon mark shows next to those rows.
time-card.a4: Hours above the weekly threshold, 40 by default, are overtime and paid at the multiplier, 1.5 by default. Overtime rules differ by country and contract; set the threshold and multiplier to match yours.
time-card.q5: How do I convert hours and minutes to decimal hours?
time-card.a5: Divide the minutes by 60: 7:30 is 7.5 hours, 7:45 is 7.75. The totals show both forms.

electricity.a1: Watts × hours a day ÷ 1000 gives kWh a day; kWh × your price per kWh gives the cost. A 1000 W air conditioner for 8 hours uses 8 kWh; at 0.15 a kWh that is 1.20 a day.
electricity.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
electricity.q3: Where do I find the watts?
electricity.a3: On the label or plug of the appliance, or in its manual. Devices that cycle on and off, like fridges and air conditioners, draw full power only part of the time, so their real use is usually lower than the label.
electricity.q4: Where do I find my price per kWh?
electricity.a4: On your electricity bill: total energy charge divided by kWh used. Tiered or time-of-use tariffs have several prices; use the one for the hours the appliance runs.
electricity.a5: Enter the standby watts (often 0.5–5 W) with 24 hours a day. 5 W all year is about 44 kWh.

ovulation.q1: How is the ovulation day estimated?
ovulation.a1: Ovulation usually happens about 14 days before the next period. With a 28-day cycle that is day 14; with a 32-day cycle, day 18.
ovulation.a2: No. The dates stay in this tab and are not stored.
ovulation.a3: The five days before ovulation plus ovulation day. Sperm can survive up to five days and the egg about a day, so these six days carry the highest chance of pregnancy.
ovulation.q4: Can I use this as contraception?
ovulation.a4: No. Cycles vary, and calendar estimates miss many ovulations. Use a reliable method of contraception, and ask a doctor if you are planning a pregnancy.
ovulation.q5: My cycle is irregular. Will it work?
ovulation.a5: Less well. Use the average length of your last six cycles. Ovulation tests or basal temperature tracking give a better signal for irregular cycles.

macro.a1: The calorie target is split by percentages and divided by calories per gram: protein 4, fat 9, carbohydrate 4. 2500 kcal at 30/30/40 is 188 g protein, 83 g fat and 250 g carbs.
macro.a2: No. The numbers stay in this tab.
macro.q3: Where does the calorie target come from?
macro.a3: Use your maintenance calories (TDEE). The TDEE calculator on cv.cm estimates it; the goal then subtracts 500 kcal to lose weight or adds 300 to gain.
macro.a4: Balanced (30/30/40) suits most people. High protein (40/30/30) helps keep muscle while losing weight. Low carb (35/45/20) suits people who prefer fewer carbohydrates.
macro.q5: How much protein do I need?
macro.a5: Active adults often aim for 1.6–2.2 g per kg of body weight. Enter your weight to see the protein per kg for the chosen split.

calories-burned.a1: Calories = MET × body weight in kg × hours. A MET is the energy of an activity relative to rest. Brisk walking is 4.3 MET, so 30 minutes at 70 kg burns about 151 kcal.
calories-burned.a2: No. The math runs in this tab.
calories-burned.q3: Where do the MET values come from?
calories-burned.a3: From the 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities (Ainsworth et al.), the standard reference used in research and fitness apps.
calories-burned.a4: Within about 20% for most people. Fitness, effort, terrain and body composition all change the real number. Treat it as an estimate.
calories-burned.q5: Does it include calories I would burn anyway?
calories-burned.a5: Yes. MET includes resting energy. Subtract about 1 kcal per kg per hour to see only the extra calories from the activity.

remove-background.a1: Yes. There is no sign-up, watermark or limit. The AI model downloads once and then runs on your own device.
remove-background.a2: No. The model runs in this browser tab with WebGPU or WebAssembly. Photos never leave your device, and closing the tab discards them.
remove-background.a3: Clear subjects: people, products, pets, cars, furniture. Fine hair and glass are harder; a plain, contrasting background helps.
remove-background.q4: Can I remove backgrounds from many images at once?
remove-background.a4: Yes. Drop several photos; they are processed one after another, and Download all saves a ZIP.
remove-background.q5: Can I put a new background behind the subject?
remove-background.a5: Choose transparent, white, any color, or a blurred copy of the original. Transparent needs PNG or WebP; JPG adds white.

image-upscaler.q1: How does the AI upscaler work?
image-upscaler.a1: It runs Real-ESRGAN, a super-resolution network, on your GPU or CPU. It enlarges 4× and redraws edges and textures; 2× averages that down for a cleaner result.
image-upscaler.a2: No. The 2–5 MB model downloads once; the image is processed in this tab and never leaves your device.
image-upscaler.a3: Up to about 16 megapixels (for example 4096 × 4096), the limit Safari can draw. Bigger inputs are scaled to fit first.
image-upscaler.a4: Photo suits camera pictures and screenshots. Anime / art keeps flat colors and outlines in illustrations, comics and game art.
image-upscaler.q5: Can it recover details that were never there?
image-upscaler.a5: No upscaler can. It makes pictures sharper and cleaner, but small text or faces it cannot see are guessed, not restored.

speech-to-text.q1: Is this speech to text free?
speech-to-text.a1: Yes, with no sign-up or minutes limit. It uses OpenAI's open Whisper model, which downloads once and runs on your device.
speech-to-text.a2: No. Audio and video are decoded and transcribed in this tab. Nothing is sent to a server, which suits private meetings and interviews.
speech-to-text.a3: Whisper knows 99 languages, including English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Indonesian and Spanish. It can detect the language or translate the speech into English.
speech-to-text.a4: Yes. Download SRT or VTT with timestamps for YouTube, Premiere, CapCut or a video player, or plain TXT.
speech-to-text.q5: How long can a file be?
speech-to-text.a5: Hours are fine; the audio is read in 30-second windows. Speed depends on your device: with a GPU, an hour usually takes a few minutes.

depth-map.a1: A grayscale image where brightness shows distance: near is white, far is black. 3D tools use it for parallax, depth of field and relighting.
depth-map.a2: Depth Anything V2 Small (Apache-2.0). It downloads once (about 25–100 MB, depending on your device) and runs in this tab.
depth-map.a3: No. The photo is processed in your browser and never leaves your device.
depth-map.q4: Can I use it with ControlNet or Blender?
depth-map.a4: Yes. Download the grayscale PNG for a ControlNet depth input, a Blender displacement map or a 3D photo effect.
