depth-map.a5: No. It is relative depth: it orders what is nearer or farther, not measured distance.

wheel.a1: Yes. The winner is drawn with Web Crypto before the wheel moves, and every entry has the same chance. The spin only shows the result.
wheel.a2: Type one name or option per line in the list. Up to 100 entries; repeat a line to give it a bigger slice.
wheel.a3: Tick “Remove the winner after each spin” to draw names one by one without repeats, for example to set a speaking order.
wheel.a4: No. The list and the draw stay in this tab.
wheel.q5: Can I use it for a giveaway?
wheel.a5: Yes, for casual draws. Share your screen while you spin. For draws with legal rules, follow the rules where you live.

average.q1: What is the difference between mean, median and mode?
average.a1: The mean is the sum divided by the count. The median is the middle value after sorting (the mean of the two middle values for an even count). The mode is the value that appears most often.
average.a2: Use the sample value (divides by n − 1) when your numbers are a sample of a bigger group, and the population value (divides by n) when they are the whole group.
average.a3: Separate them with spaces, new lines or semicolons. With the decimal mark set to a dot (3.5), commas separate numbers too; set it to a comma for 3,5. You can paste a column from a spreadsheet.
average.a4: When every value appears the same number of times, for example all different, no value is the mode.
average.a5: No. The numbers stay in this tab.

metronome.q1: How do I use the metronome?
metronome.a1: Set the BPM, choose the beats per bar and press Start. The first beat of each bar is higher when the accent is on.
metronome.a2: Press Tap in time with a song four or more times; the BPM follows the average of your last taps. A pause of two seconds starts over.
metronome.a3: Clicks are scheduled on the Web Audio clock, not with timers, so they stay steady even when the page is busy.
metronome.a4: Check the volume slider, the device volume and the silent switch on phones. Some browsers pause audio in background tabs.
metronome.q5: What do Andante and Allegro mean?
metronome.a5: They are Italian tempo marks. Andante is a walking pace (about 76–108 BPM), Allegro is fast (about 120–156 BPM).

keyboard-test.q1: How do I test my keyboard?
keyboard-test.a1: Click the keyboard picture, then press every key. Keys that work turn pink; the one you are holding turns dark.
keyboard-test.q2: A key does not light up. Is it broken?
keyboard-test.a2: Not always. Fn, some media keys and keys the system reserves (like Print Screen on some computers) never reach the browser. Try the key in a text field too.
keyboard-test.a3: How many keys the keyboard reports at once. Hold several keys together; “Most at once” shows the highest number seen.
keyboard-test.q4: What do key, code and keyCode mean?
keyboard-test.a4: key is the character or name the key produces, code is the physical key position, and keyCode is the older numeric code many games still use.
keyboard-test.a5: No. Key presses are shown in this tab only and are not sent anywhere.

zodiac.a1: Enter your birthday. The tool shows your star sign (Western zodiac), its date range and element.
zodiac.q2: What is my Chinese zodiac animal?
zodiac.a2: It follows the lunar year, which starts on Lunar New Year between 21 January and 20 February. If you were born before that day, your animal is the previous year’s.
zodiac.q3: Why do sign dates differ between sites?
zodiac.a3: The Sun enters each sign at a slightly different time each year, so the first day can move by one. If you were born on the edge, check an ephemeris for your birth year.
zodiac.a4: In the Chinese calendar each year has an element (wood, fire, earth, metal or water) and is yin or yang; together with the animal they give the 60-year cycle, such as 甲辰 (wood dragon) for 2024.
zodiac.a5: No. The date stays in this tab.

chmod.title: Chmod calculator
chmod.privacyNote: Works in this tab. Nothing is uploaded, and no file is changed.
chmod.recursiveWarn: -R gives files and folders the same number: 644 removes x from folders (you can no longer open them) and 755 makes every file executable. This version uses a capital X, so folders stay enterable and files keep execute only if they already had it:
chmod.dirHint: For a folder (or -R) without special bits the command uses 00755: GNU chmod keeps a folder's setuid/setgid unless the number has that extra leading 0; macOS reads it as 0755.
chmod.quoteHint: The name is taken literally: spaces, quotes, $ ; & and also * ? [ ] are quoted, so a file such as Movie [1080p].mkv matches. Only a leading ~/ stays unquoted for your home folder. A name starting with - gets -- first.
chmod.badOctal: Octal needs 3 or 4 digits from 0 to 7.
chmod.badSymbolic: Use 9 characters such as rwxr-xr-x (s, S, t or T for special bits).
